commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Honor the CrossEncoder activation saved by Sentence Transformers v6
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Sentence Transformers v6 saves a CrossEncoder's `activation_fn` in `config_sentence_transformers.json` instead of `config.json`, but vLLM only reads the `config.json` keys. Rerankers saved this way with an `Identity` activation are therefore scored with the default sigmoid instead of returning raw logits. This reads the saved setting in `get_config` and sets it as the default activation before `hf_overrides` are applied. It is only used for plain CrossEncoders whose ST pipeline is a single Transformer module.

## Claims

- `/score`, `/rerank` and `/classify` apply the activation that plain ST CrossEncoders declare in `config_sentence_transformers.json`, matching `CrossEncoder.predict`.
- `hf_overrides` still win, as a dict or a callable, through `sentence_transformers.activation_fn` or `sbert_ce_default_activation_function`. A callable runs on the real config, with the saved activation already set. Without an override, the saved activation is preferred over both `config.json` keys, as in Sentence Transformers. `problem_type` keeps its existing priority in vLLM.
- **Behavior change for `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2`.** It declares `activation_fn: Identity`, so vLLM now returns its logits instead of sigmoid scores. This matches `CrossEncoder.predict` and its model card ("Each value corresponds to a raw logit"). Rankings don't change. Its reranker test in `tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py` (nightly) now compares against the HF logits, and has a second case that sets the Sigmoid override below and compares against their sigmoid. To keep the old scores, pass `--hf-overrides '{"sbert_ce_default_activation_function": "torch.nn.modules.activation.Sigmoid"}'`. The scoring docs have a migration note with this setting ("Activation function" in `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md`).
- No change for other models: of the 133 Hub models named in the pooling tests, only that one and `polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm` declare an activation, and zerank's saved `Sigmoid` gives the same sigmoid as on `main`. Qwen3-Reranker, Qwen3-VL-Reranker and jina-reranker-m0 save `activation_fn: Identity` on top of a `LogitScore` or custom module that vLLM scores itself, so they are skipped.

## Validation

Offline `LLM.score` on RTX 4090 (`enforce_eager=True`), one query and three documents, compared with `sentence_transformers.CrossEncoder.predict` (CPU) and vLLM `main`. The ettin and unchanged-model tables were run on 913439972d against `main` at cb59326aee, before the latest merge of `main`; the Nemotron results are from the current head. The script is at the end of this section. "Sigmoid" is `torch.nn.modules.activation.Sigmoid`.

`tomaarsen/ettin-encoder-150m-reranker-msmarco524k-1e-4-20261014` (ST v6, `activation_fn: Identity`, single label, single Transformer module). Sentence Transformers gives 8.3557 / -7.0466 / -8.0292, and 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 with `activation_fn=torch.nn.Sigmoid()`.

| `hf_overrides` | vLLM `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| none | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 8.3582 / -7.0457 / -8.0270 |
| dict, `sentence_transformers.activation_fn` = Sigmoid | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| dict, `sbert_ce_default_activation_function` = Sigmoid | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable setting `sentence_transformers.activation_fn` | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable setting `sbert_ce_default_activation_function` | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable: Sigmoid if `config.num_labels == 1` | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| same, setting the legacy key | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable: Sigmoid if `config.architectures[0]` ends with `ForSequenceClassification` | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable returning the config unchanged | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 8.3626 / -7.0483 / -8.0284 |

Repeated runs of the same mode give one of 8.3582 / -7.0457 / -8.0270, 8.3612 / -7.0483 / -8.0342 or 8.3626 / -7.0483 / -8.0284 for the raw logits. The sigmoid rows don't change.

The previous head (98606eab71) got the conditional callables wrong, as found in review: checking `get_act_fn` on the resulting `ModelConfig`, both `num_labels` callables gave `Identity` and the `architectures` one raised `TypeError`. On this head they give the sigmoid, and every row above matches `main` except "none" and "returning the config unchanged".

A local copy of the same checkpoint whose `config.json` also has an older `"sentence_transformers": {"activation_fn": "torch.nn.modules.activation.Sigmoid"}`. Sentence Transformers still uses the saved `Identity` (8.3557 / -7.0466 / -8.0292):

| `hf_overrides` | vLLM `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| none | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 8.3612 / -7.0483 / -8.0342 |
| dict, either key = Sigmoid | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable setting the legacy key, unconditionally or if `num_labels == 1` | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 |
| callable returning the config unchanged | 0.9998 / 0.0009 / 0.0003 | 8.3612 / -7.0483 / -8.0342 |

`nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2`, `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py -k reranker` (fp16, 2% tolerance), on the current head, which has `main` at 62902f6ce6 merged in. `test_reranker` now has two cases: `logits` uses no override and compares with the HF logits, and `sigmoid` uses the `--hf-overrides` setting from the migration note and compares with the sigmoid of the HF logits.

| Input | HF logit | vLLM, `logits` case | sigmoid(HF logit) | vLLM, `sigmoid` case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| text document 1 | -0.7637 | -0.7615 | 0.317850 | 0.318325 |
| text document 2 | -7.7109 | -7.7105 | 0.000448 | 0.000448 |
| image document 1 | -2.5801 | -2.5818 | 0.070432 | 0.070317 |
| image document 2 | -5.4023 | -5.4046 | 0.004486 | 0.004476 |

- This PR: both cases pass 3/3. Over repeated runs the relative difference is at most 0.35% for `logits` and 0.24% for `sigmoid`. Text document 1 varies between runs: -0.7615 or -0.7664 in the `logits` case, 0.317265 or 0.318325 in the `sigmoid` case.
- With `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` from `main` (62902f6ce6): `sigmoid` passes, and `logits` fails as expected with `HF=-0.7637` vs `vLLM=0.3183`. Without the override, `main` gives 0.317265 / 0.000447 / 0.070317 / 0.004476, the same scores as this PR with it. The override also works on `main`, so it can be set before upgrading.
- The flags exactly as written in the docs (`--runner pooling --trust-remote-code --hf-overrides '{...}'`), parsed with `EngineArgs`, resolve to `PoolerClassify` (sigmoid). Without the override, this PR resolves to `PoolerIdentity`.

Unchanged models (`main` vs this PR):

| Model | Saved metadata | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cross-encoder/ms-marco-TinyBERT-L2-v2` | legacy `Identity` in `config.json` | 7.1903 / -6.2825 / -11.5624 | identical |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B` | ST 5.4 `Identity` + `LogitScore` | 0.9155 / 0.8633 / 0.3493 | 0.9105 / 0.8660 / 0.3461, the other of the two results it alternates between on `main` too |

Also on this PR, `get_act_fn` on the `ModelConfig` for TinyBERT under every override mode above, for `zerank-2-reranker-vllm`, and for Qwen3-Reranker: same as `main`.

Tests:

- `pytest tests/test_config.py`: 509 passed, 7 skipped, 3 failed (`test_rope_customization`, `test_is_encoder_decoder[meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-False]`, `test_eagle_draft_model_config`). All three need gated Llama checkpoints and fail on `main` too.
- `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_activations.py tests/transformers_utils`: 159 passed, 1 failed (`test_get_llama3_eos_token`, gated Llama checkpoint, fails on `main` too).
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

<details>
<summary>Offline script</summary>

`st_models.py` (vLLM): `python st_models.py <model> <mode> <tag>`

```python
import sys

QUERY = "How many people live in Berlin?"
DOCS = [
    "Berlin has a population of 3,520,031 registered inhabitants.",
    "Berlin is well known for its museums.",
    "New York City is famous for the Metropolitan Museum of Art.",
]
SIGMOID = "torch.nn.modules.activation.Sigmoid"


def set_sigmoid(hf_config):
    hf_config.sentence_transformers = {"activation_fn": SIGMOID}
    return hf_config


def set_sigmoid_legacy(hf_config):
    hf_config.sbert_ce_default_activation_function = SIGMOID
    return hf_config


def sigmoid_if_single_label(hf_config):
    if hf_config.num_labels == 1:
        hf_config.sentence_transformers = {"activation_fn": SIGMOID}
    return hf_config


def sigmoid_if_single_label_legacy(hf_config):
    if hf_config.num_labels == 1:
        hf_config.sbert_ce_default_activation_function = SIGMOID
    return hf_config


def sigmoid_by_architecture(hf_config):
    if hf_config.architectures[0].endswith("ForSequenceClassification"):
        hf_config.sentence_transformers = {"activation_fn": SIGMOID}
    return hf_config


def passthrough(hf_config):
    return hf_config


OVERRIDES = {
    "none": None,
    "dict": {"sentence_transformers": {"activation_fn": SIGMOID}},
    "dict-legacy": {"sbert_ce_default_activation_function": SIGMOID},
    "fn": set_sigmoid,
    "fn-legacy": set_sigmoid_legacy,
    "fn-num-labels": sigmoid_if_single_label,
    "fn-num-labels-legacy": sigmoid_if_single_label_legacy,
    "fn-architecture": sigmoid_by_architecture,
    "fn-passthrough": passthrough,
    "qwen3": {
        "architectures": ["Qwen3ForSequenceClassification"],
        "classifier_from_token": ["no", "yes"],
        "is_original_qwen3_reranker": True,
    },
}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    model, mode, tag = sys.argv[1:4]
    from vllm import LLM

    llm = LLM(
        model=model,
        runner="pooling",
        max_model_len=512,
        kv_cache_memory_bytes=1 << 30,
        enforce_eager=True,
        hf_overrides=OVERRIDES[mode],
    )
    scores = [round(o.outputs.score, 4) for o in llm.score(QUERY, DOCS)]
    print(f"RESULT\t{tag}\t{model}\t{mode}\t{scores}")
```

`st_ref.py` (Sentence Transformers): `python st_ref.py <model>...`

```python
"""Sentence Transformers reference scores (CPU), default and with Sigmoid."""

import sys

import torch
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

from st_models import DOCS, QUERY

for model in sys.argv[1:]:
    for mode, kwargs in (("none", {}), ("sigmoid", {"activation_fn": torch.nn.Sigmoid()})):
        ce = CrossEncoder(model, device="cpu", **kwargs)
        scores = [round(float(s), 4) for s in ce.predict([(QUERY, d) for d in DOCS])]
        print(
            f"RESULT\tST\t{model.split('/')[-1][:28]}\t{mode}\t{scores}"
            f"\t({type(ce.activation_fn).__name__})"
        )
```

The local copy symlinks every file of the ettin snapshot except `config.json`, which gets the `sentence_transformers` key added.

</details>

## Details

`get_act_fn` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/activations.py`) reads `config.sentence_transformers["activation_fn"]` first and the legacy `sbert_ce_default_activation_function` second. Sentence Transformers writes `activation_fn` to `config_sentence_transformers.json` on save (`CrossEncoder._get_model_config`) and reads it from there first (`CrossEncoder._parse_model_config`). It falls back to the `config.json` keys only when that file has no value.

The fix adds a cached `get_sentence_transformers_activation_fn` next to `get_sentence_transformers_chat_template_kwargs`. When it returns a value, `get_config` does two things right before applying `hf_overrides`:

- It sets the value as `sbert_ce_default_activation_function`. That is the key `get_act_fn` checks last, so a dict or callable override of either key still wins, and a callable sees the real config.
- It drops an older `sentence_transformers.activation_fn` from `config.json`, because Sentence Transformers prefers the saved value over it.

The pooler code is unchanged and the existing `torch.nn.modules.` restriction still applies.

- ST applies the activation to the output of the last module. That only matches the classifier output vLLM computes when the pipeline is a single Transformer module (`_ST_TRANSFORMER_MODULE_TYPES`), so `modules.json` is checked as well.
- `get_config` runs for every model. The helper therefore first checks that `config_sentence_transformers.json` exists with `file_or_path_exists`, like the `hf_quant_config.json` check above it, so other models don't get an extra download request. The files are read from the same place as `config.json` (`hf_config_path` if set).

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR for this (searched "config_sentence_transformers activation_fn", "CrossEncoder activation_fn", "sentence transformers v6 cross encoder", "reranker sigmoid Identity"). #31563 (closed, unmerged) and #60877 handled ST v6 reranker chat templates, not the activation.

AI assistance was used to find this bug, write the fix, and run the validation shown above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Bugfix] Read sliding_window from ManagerConfig.params in voxtral realtime test
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`test_voxtral_realtime.py::test_voxtral_realtime_forward` fails on main in nightly build [102399](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102399), on both `(H200 MIG 35GB) [Nightly] Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` and its MI355 mirror:

```
E       AttributeError: 'ManagerConfig' object has no attribute 'sliding_window'
models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py:94: AttributeError
```

#61452 moved KV cache policy into `ManagerConfig` and rewrote this assertion from `spec.sliding_window` to `manager_config.sliding_window`. The window is now a manager parameter, so it lives at `manager_config.params.sliding_window`. The model side is already correct: `whisper_causal.py` sets it with `sw_config.replace_params(sliding_window=pooled)`. This is a one-line test fix.

I grepped `vllm/` and `tests/` for other `.sliding_window` reads off a `ManagerConfig` that skip `.params` and found none.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for "voxtral sliding_window" and "ManagerConfig sliding_window". The only related result, #67420, fixes a different #61452 fallout (`test_umbp_lazy.py` imports).

## Test Plan

- CI: `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-1` (NVIDIA + MI355 mirror), run as a selected-steps build on this PR.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (pinned 0.17.2) on the changed file. pre-commit hooks ran on commit.

## Test Result

- ruff and pre-commit pass.
- GPU results will be added below once the selected-steps build finishes.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Consistent drafted, verified and accepted token counts
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Summary

Implements RFC #64099. Builds on #58340 and keeps its 11 commits.

Spec decode now reports three counts:

- **`drafted`**: tokens that came out of the drafter, including grammar-invalid ones.
- **`verified` (new)**: drafted tokens that went into the target forward pass.
- **`accepted`**: unchanged.

`drafted >= verified >= accepted` holds in total and at every step. `verified` is reported wherever the other two are: Prometheus, the log line, per-request metrics, `vllm bench serve` (Python and Rust) and the Rust frontend.

## What changes for users

- New counters `vllm:spec_decode_num_verified_tokens` and `vllm:spec_decode_num_verified_tokens_per_pos`, and per-request fields `num_verified_tokens` and `per_step_verified`.
- With structured outputs, `drafted` now includes grammar-invalid draft tokens (#29821 subtracted them), so `accepted / drafted` goes down.
- ~~MRV1 `ngram_gpu` no longer counts its `-1` padding as `drafted`, so `accepted / drafted` goes up and matches CPU `ngram`.~~

## How it works

- Only the worker sees both the drafter's output and the target forward pass, so the model runner reports both counts per request in `ModelRunnerOutput` (`num_drafted_tokens_per_req`, `num_verified_tokens_per_req`). The scheduler only counts `accepted`.
- MRV2 counts the non `-1` draft tokens on the GPU before the drafter overwrites them. ~~MRV1 records the count when the drafter proposes (the valid count for `ngram_gpu`).~~
- `verified` is the draft tokens in the forward pass, capped at `drafted`. With adaptive verification (AV) it includes the AV budget.
- Out-of-tree model runners, and MRV2 diffusion models (no drafter), don't report the counts. The scheduler then counts the scheduled draft tokens, as on main.
- Only the stats change. The rollback of `num_computed_tokens` still uses the scheduled count.

## RFC corrections and differences

- **Sync SO schedules the first grammar-invalid draft token** (#61557). So "sync, grammar rejects last 2" has `verified` 3 (not 2), and "sync, grammar rejects all 4" has `verified` 1 and the step is counted.
- **Truncated drafts** (e.g. near `max_model_len`) still count as `drafted`. The RFC excludes them.
- **`num_spec_steps`**: ~~a step where MRV1 `ngram_gpu` finds no match is counted with 0 `drafted`, except with sync SO, where it is not scheduled.~~ A grammar that already terminated is skipped in sync and counted in async.

Out of scope (see the RFC): draft tokens after a stop (#56101), and zero draft tokens when the drafter is skipped (#34734). The fixes proposed for them (#56137, #56195 and #34757) are compatible with the invariant: they leave `drafted` and `verified` unchanged, or drop the step from all three counts.

## Validation

- **e2e invariant check** on 1x H100, 12 configs at `97b1d9dc37` (~~MRV1 and~~ MRV2, sync and async, `ngram_gpu`, ~~CPU `ngram`,~~ EAGLE-3, DSpark with and without AV, Rust frontend, both bench clients).
- **New CI check**: `test_async_scheduling.py` now asserts `drafted >= verified >= accepted` on the counter deltas of every spec decode run (EAGLE-3 and `ngram_gpu`, sync and async, JSON schema, preemption, chunked prefill). It passes at `97b1d9dc37` (`ngram_gpu` also with ~~MRV1 and~~ MRV2 forced).
- **Unit tests**: `tests/v1/core`, `tests/v1/metrics`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_request_acceptance.py` pass. `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders` fails on main too.
- **Other GPU tests**: entrypoint tests at `97b1d9dc37`. At `09206e80a1`: `test_async_scheduling.py` and `test_async_scheduling_accuracy.py` (`-k "eagle3 or ngram_gpu"`), `ngram_suffix`, `test_ngram_gpu.py`, `aux_output_connector/test_store.py` pass.
- **Rust**: fmt and clippy clean, touched crates pass. 5 `vllm-chat` / `vllm-text` snapshot tests fail on main too.

<details>
<summary>e2e invariant check details</summary>

Temperature 0. Each server gets one JSON-schema request and one free-text request. The check asserts `drafted >= verified >= accepted` at every step of the `detailed` payload and on the Prometheus deltas, and that the `_per_pos` `verified` counters sum to the `verified` total. With AV, it also asserts `verified < drafted`.

```bash
# ngram_gpu
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --speculative-config '{"method": "ngram_gpu", "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "prompt_lookup_min": 1, "prompt_lookup_max": 3}' --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log --no-async-scheduling  # or --async-scheduling
# EAGLE-3
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log --async-scheduling  # or --no-async-scheduling
# DSpark with or without AV, optionally VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}' --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log --no-async-scheduling  # or --async-scheduling
```

Each cell is `num_spec_steps` / `drafted` / `verified` / `accepted`:

| Config | JSON schema | Free text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ~~MRV1 `ngram_gpu`, sync~~ | ~~10 / 40 / 23 / 12~~ | ~~228 / 520 / 520 / 71~~ |
| ~~MRV1 `ngram_gpu`, async~~ | ~~19 / 40 / 40 / 12~~ | ~~228 / 520 / 520 / 71~~ |
| ~~MRV1 CPU `ngram`, sync~~ | ~~10 / 40 / 23 / 12~~ | ~~130 / 520 / 520 / 71~~ |
| ~~MRV1 EAGLE-3, sync~~ | ~~43 / 129 / 125 / 120~~ | ~~130 / 390 / 390 / 170~~ |
| ~~MRV1 EAGLE-3, async~~ | ~~43 / 129 / 129 / 121~~ | ~~132 / 396 / 396 / 168~~ |
| MRV2 `ngram_gpu`, sync | 19 / 76 / 35 / 12 | 228 / 912 / 912 / 71 |
| MRV2 `ngram_gpu`, async | 19 / 76 / 76 / 12 | 228 / 912 / 912 / 71 |
| MRV2 EAGLE-3, async | 43 / 129 / 129 / 121 | 130 / 390 / 390 / 170 |
| MRV2 DSpark, async | 36 / 252 / 252 / 126 | 71 / 497 / 497 / 228 |
| MRV2 DSpark + AV, sync | 36 / 252 / 194 / 126 | 78 / 546 / 382 / 221 |
| MRV2 DSpark + AV, async | 36 / 252 / 252 / 126 | 78 / 546 / 378 / 221 |
| MRV2 DSpark + AV, async, Rust frontend | 36 / 252 / 252 / 126 | 78 / 546 / 378 / 221 |

- ~~MRV1 `ngram_gpu` and CPU `ngram` report the same counts. `ngram_gpu` also counts steps without a match (0 `drafted`).~~ MRV2 `ngram_gpu` fills unmatched slots with the last sampled token, so it drafts 4 tokens per step.
- Sync and async report the same `drafted` and acceptance rate. Only `verified` differs, because sync drops grammar-invalid draft tokens before the forward pass.
- With AV, `verified` is well below `drafted` on free text.
- `vllm bench serve` (Python, and Rust with `VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1`) prints `Verified tokens:` and saves `spec_decode_verified_tokens`.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Model] Use FlashInfer for Gemma 4 with an NVFP4 KV cache when FA4 is unavailable
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Without FA4, `Gemma4Config` pins `TRITON_ATTN` for Gemma 4's heterogeneous head dimensions. Triton cannot read an NVFP4 KV cache, so `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on these GPUs fails at backend selection unless `--attention-backend FLASHINFER` is passed by hand, as in the SM121 run on [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963). Since #46963, FlashInfer reads that cache on SM8x and SM12x. This pins `FLASHINFER` instead for a plain Gemma 4 architecture with an `nvfp4` cache.

## Claims

- On SM8x and SM12x, which have no FA4 and where FlashInfer reads an NVFP4 cache, a plain Gemma 4 model that does not need multimodal-prefix attention (text-only, or a checkpoint that is not a multimodal-prefix LM) starts on FlashInfer with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` when no backend is set.
- In that same branch, every other cache dtype, including `nvfp4_4over6`, still gets `TRITON_ATTN`, and so do DiffusionGemma and EmbeddingGemma2, which call `Gemma4Config`. An explicitly set backend is left as is.
- No change where FA4 is available.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py
```

The new `test_gemma4_without_fa4_backend` covers the FA4-less branch for the three plain Gemma 4 cases and both models that reuse it. Its `nvfp4` case fails on `main`. The five cases pass with stock FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and 0.7.1rc5.

End to end on SM80 with stock `flashinfer-python==0.7.1rc5` and `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` (heads 256 + 512), four fixed prompts, greedy, 64 tokens:

| | `main` | `main` + `--attention-backend FLASHINFER` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` | fails: `TRITON_ATTN ... kv_cache_dtype not supported` | runs | runs on FlashInfer |

With stock FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5, the PR default and explicit FlashInfer matched token IDs on all four raw and four chat prompts when reusing the same torch.compile artifacts. A fresh-compilation main run differed on two chat prompts from a cached main run; the cause was not isolated. The same routing change was also validated on October 8 with stock FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, main's pin at the time: four raw and four chat prompts matched the explicit FlashInfer baseline.

## Details

#46329 also routes Gemma 4 with an NVFP4 cache to FlashInfer, as part of a two-pass V split, calibration support and image masking behind new environment variables. This change is only the routing: it uses the existing FlashInfer path, adds no environment variable or backend code, and is limited to plain Gemma 4 with an `nvfp4` cache so the policies of the models that reuse `Gemma4Config` stay as they are.

A Gemma 4 checkpoint that runs as a multimodal-prefix LM, such as `gemma-4-31B-it` with images enabled, relies on FlashInfer mm-prefix support, which #46558 has since added to main; the runs above cover text-only launches only.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Render tool-result media in the Inkling renderer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vllm-project/vllm#66891 taught the Python Inkling renderer to render tool results that carry media, such as a screenshot returned by a tool. The Rust Inkling renderer flattens tool-response content to text, so the same request fails with a 400 (`image_url` / `input_audio` content is not supported). This PR renders tool-result media in the Rust Inkling renderer with Python's framing.

## Claims

- A tool message with image or audio parts renders on the Rust frontend for Inkling: each media part becomes its own `<|message_tool|>` block with the tool's author name, holding only the media marker the multimodal processor expands, token for token as in Python.
- Adjacent text parts coalesce into one text block, so a text-only result keeps its single-block framing; an empty result (`""` or `[]`) still writes an empty text block, so the tool call it answers is not left dangling.
- User and system messages render unchanged; video and `tool_reference` parts stay errors, as on other roles.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `ab72c466aa`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2687 tests run: 2686 passed, 1 failed, 13 skipped
```

The one failure, `vllm-server` `routes::tests::request_id_header_is_absent_by_default` (503 instead of 200 from `/health`), fails the same way on `main` (`ab72c466aa`) and is unrelated to this change; vllm-project/vllm#67409 fixes the fixture behind it.

Tests:

- `renders_tool_response_media_and_coalesces_text_parts` ports the Python unit tests in `tests/renderers/test_inkling.py` as cases of one fixture (`tool_media_input.json` → `tool_media_output.txt`), each block matching the Python expected string: `test_tool_response_image_part`, `test_tool_response_image_marker_per_part`, `test_tool_response_multiple_text_parts`, `test_tool_response_coalesces_text_around_media`, `test_tool_response_empty_still_emits_block` (the `[]` case; `""` was already covered) and `test_tool_response_audio_part`. With the renderer change reverted it fails with `UnsupportedMultimodalContent("image_url")`.
- `rejects_tool_response_video` pins that video stays an error on the new path.
- The Python renderer renders the new fixture to the same complete token sequence. The evidence reaches the rendered prompt token IDs; no HTTP or real-checkpoint run.

## Details

`InklingChatRenderer::write_tool_response` walks the content parts with Python's coalescing rule: text parts accumulate into one pending block, and each media part flushes the pending text and writes its own block. The image and audio block writers now take the author name (user and system messages pass `None`, so their output is unchanged), and the per-part `match` of `write_chat_content` moves into `write_part_block` so both paths share it.

**Layering.** The consumer is the Inkling renderer itself: it produces the prompt token IDs, including the media markers. Media collection needs no change: with `media_order: None`, `vllm-chat` already collects media from `ChatMessage::ToolResponse` parts in message order, which is the order the renderer now writes the markers in. The DTO already accepts media in tool messages (`MessageContent`, shared with user messages).

**Behavior left as is.** Python takes the tool's author name from `message.name` first; Rust keeps resolving it from `tool_call_id`, since Rust's chat messages do not carry `name` yet.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes the Rust Inkling renderer's tool responses. vllm-project/vllm#67325 adds a separate Inkling 2 renderer (`renderer/inkling/inkling2.rs`) and does not touch this one.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

## Claims

- The recipes site renders the configuration InferenceX #5036 benchmarks on MI355X:
  - two GPUs per server (`--data-parallel-size 2`), attention DP2 with the MoE tensor-parallel across both ranks (`--enable-expert-parallel` removed), behind the consistent-hash vLLM Router;
  - UMBP KV offload (`UMBPStoreConnector`, standalone server tab);
  - `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` (#66036), `--prefill-schedule-interval 11`, Engram tables in host memory, 16384-token prefill budget, cudagraph capture up to 1024;
  - concurrency points 128, 256 and 384 on the nightly carrying #64715 and #66036; the 128 point sets `kv_offload: off`, as InferenceX runs it without offloading.
- `kv_offload_support: { umbp: verified }` makes the opt-in UMBP option available for this model.

## Validation

- From a vllm-project/recipes checkout with the `umbp` option, `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this branch>/recipes` passes: `✓ vllm recipes … are valid against the renderer`.
- The rendered command matches the InferenceX recipe flag for flag: the per-point `vllm serve` / `docker run`, the UMBP Server companion (socket address equal to the connector `endpoint`) and the vLLM Router (`--intra-node-data-parallel-size 2`). At 128 the command has no `--kv-transfer-config` and no UMBP Server tab; 256 and 384 have both. `pnpm test:presets` and `pnpm test:kv-offload` pass with this branch as the vLLM source.
- Local MI355X AgentX replays (agentx-fast, 1200 s, single runs) of this configuration on the default `fp8_ds_mla` KV and an earlier nightly, against the same configuration without offloading:

  | Concurrency | Total tok/s/GPU, no offload → UMBP | Prompt tokens restored from UMBP |

  | 384 | 143,888 → 291,619 (+103%) | 21.5% |

  The `fp8_e4m3` KV cache and the pinned nightly are qualified by the InferenceX sweep of #5036.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Preserve values from non-native-endian NumPy embeddings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Allow image and video embedding readers to consume NumPy `.npy` arrays whose byte order differs from the host, preserving their values and dtype.

## Claims

- Normalize a non-native NumPy dtype to native byte order before constructing a Torch tensor.
- Use the same conversion for image/video bytes, base64, and file loading.
- Keep the native-endian `torch.from_numpy` path and the existing `allow_pickle=False` behavior.

## Validation

- [Native CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43423892421): **27 failures / 23 passes on the original source**, then **50 passes with this change**.
- **31 existing serialization and embedding tests pass.**
- [Repository pre-commit hooks and Ruff](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43423896475) pass.
- Both native-endian and big-endian input arrays are tested through the real bytes, base64, and file readers. Floating-point values and large int64 metadata are compared with independent Python-value references.
- Two saved tiny Llava cases run the actual public `LLM.generate` path. The directly constructed and decoded image embeddings produce matching token IDs and all 32 vocabulary log probabilities.

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_numpy_embedding_byteorder.py
```

## Details

A `.npy` file carries its dtype and byte order. `np.load` correctly reads a big-endian array, but passing that array directly to `torch.from_numpy` raises an unsupported-byte-order error on a little-endian host. Re-encoding with `astype(dtype.newbyteorder('='))` converts the numerical representation instead of merely relabeling the bytes.

The regression cases cover FP16/FP32/FP64, transposed/strided inputs, empty shapes, large int64 values, and object-array rejection. A saved tiny Llava model consumes an image embedding loaded through the real base64 handler and produces the same tokens and logprobs as the equivalent directly constructed tensor. Its test checkpoint uses the CLIP wrapper names supported by the native loader; the tensors and model execution are real.

The official C++ and Rust CPU runtime was built from base `191e5d5` and reused for this Python-only change. The tests run on CPU; they do not claim GPU coverage or a model-quality increase. Native-endian arrays keep the existing `torch.from_numpy` path. Foreign-endian arrays require one value-preserving conversion.

The native validation above tested commit `50abe3b5a09cd3e505762c92f2fceccf3ebdd38d`; the original DCO commit `e4ffb1f7a6e2f582cf62d567753b7a658ca86354` had the identical Git tree. After review, merge commit `53fb66896a99d60adadbb8d92008e28084487a3a` incorporated upstream `main` through `65c2b39fac461b9054759c239299d3cb571a3a6a`. All five files in this PR retain their validated blob contents. The upstream changes concern speculative-decoding validation and KV-cache tests; no C++ or Rust runtime files changed. The maintainer-authorized `/ci run` command started [upstream Buildkite CI #102481](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102481) for this merge commit.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Fix prefix_repetition crash and custom_audio --output-len in bench throughput
commits.pr_body:
This PR fixes 2 issues in `vllm bench throughput` whose bugs stem from their arguments behaving in unexpected ways. 

1. `prefix_repetition`: crashes if you leave out the --prefix-repetition-* flags, due to all flags getting set to `None`
2. `custom_audio`: if run with `--output-len 64` you want 64 output tokens for each request, but you don't get 64

## Cause

1. Since #50981, `vllm bench throughput` passes its args to the shared `get_samples` path, and `None` values are no longer dropped. The four `--prefix-repetition-*` flags default to `None` in throughput. So the below command crashes with `TypeError`

```bash
vllm bench throughput --dataset-name prefix_repetition
```

2. The same refactor stopped `--output-len` from reaching `custom_audio`, which reads only `custom_output_len`. So the below command does not work as intended

```bash
vllm bench throughput --dataset-name custom_audio --output-len 64 ...
```

## Fix

1. Default the four `--prefix-repetition-*` flags to `PrefixRepetitionRandomDataset` constants, the same values that `bench serve` uses.
2. In `_to_serve_args`, copied `--output-len` into `custom_output_len` when `--custom-output-len` is not set. This restores the order from before #50981.
3. Also, added a regression test for each fix.

## Validation

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition --num-prompts 20

pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py \
  -k "prefix_repetition_without_prefix_flags or custom_audio_output_len"
```

```text
# before
bench: exit 1, TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for //: 'int' and 'NoneType'
pytest: 2 failed, 1 passed
  TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for //: 'int' and 'NoneType'
  assert None == 64

# after
bench: exit 0, Throughput: 47.07 requests/s, 2560 output tokens (20 × 128)
pytest: 3 passed
```

The bench ran on an A100 40GB. `custom_audio` change is covered by the unit test only.

## Disclosure

**Not a duplicate**: #59881 changes only validate_args, and #57090 changes how many prompts the dataset keeps. Neither touches these defaults. I found no issue for this bug.

**AI assistance**: Claude Opus 5.5 found the bug and drafted the code. I reviewed every change and ran the tests.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In eager mode the GLM-5.3 (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower built `cu_seqlens` on the GPU and took `max_seqlen` from it, so `vit_flash_attn_wrapper`'s `max_seqlen.item()` synchronized the host in each of the 24 blocks. Second of two PRs on this tower. #67235 (q/k RMSNorm + RoPE fusion, residual inside RMSNorm) has merged, and this branch now has main merged in on top of it.

## Claims

- No host-device sync per vision block: `max_seqlen` stays a CPU tensor for every attention backend.
- Vision tower wall time −2% to −14% on 1x B200 (largest with many small images), GPU time unchanged.
- Output bit-identical to main.

## Validation

After merging main (`8a8cad0253`) the file is identical to the #67194 + #67235 combination measured in #67235, whose "#67194" column against its fused columns is that measurement; this PR's gain on top of the merged #67235 alone was not re-measured.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Bugfix] Migrate UMBP lazy offload tests to the ManagerConfig KV cache API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the collection error that has been failing `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 KV Connectors` on `main` since #61798. `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_lazy.py` still imports `FullAttentionSpec`, `SlidingWindowSpec` and `KVCacheGroupSpec`, which #61452 removed a few hours before #61798 merged.

- Failing builds: [#102401](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102401) (`519262f41`, #61798) and [#102403](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102403) (`74b2399be`); last pass [#102399](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102399) (`ab72c466a`)

```
ERROR collecting tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_lazy.py
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'FullAttentionSpec' from 'vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface'
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```

## Claims

- `test_umbp_lazy.py` imports again, so pytest collection in the V1 KV Connectors step stops aborting.
- The `:amd: (MI355 DPX) UMBP Connector Unit Tests` step runs `pytest v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_*.py`, so this also fixes its collection of this file.
- This is a test-only change. The tests still set up the same KV cache groups and keep the same assertions.

## Validation

CPU-only (`torch==2.14.0+cpu`, no GPU visible).

Before (current `main`), the error matches CI:
```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_lazy.py -q
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'FullAttentionSpec' from 'vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface'
1 warning, 1 error in 0.74s
```

After:
```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_lazy.py -q
33 passed, 1 warning in 14.28s
```
(On CPU-only torch, the global `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` teardown in `tests/conftest.py` raises on `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()`. It does this for every test, unrelated to this change, so I no-op'd it with a local pytest plugin for the run above. None of the 33 test bodies failed with or without that plugin.)

`pre-commit run --files tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_lazy.py` passes, including ruff check, ruff format, mypy and typos.

Not yet verified on AMD GPUs. The UMBP lazy tests use `BlockPool` and the scheduler with a stub handle, so they don't need a GPU or mori.

## Details

Root cause: a semantic merge conflict.
- #61452 (merged 04:47 UTC) moved KV cache allocation policy into `ManagerConfig` and deleted the per-policy spec classes and `KVCacheGroupSpec`. It migrated every existing UMBP test.
- #61798 (merged 07:21 UTC) had been written against the old API. It added `test_umbp_lazy.py` and merged cleanly at the text level, so nothing caught the stale imports.

The migration follows the pattern #61452 used in `test_umbp_hybrid.py` and `umbp_test_utils.py`:
- `FullAttentionSpec(...)` becomes `AttentionSpec(...)`. `new_kv_cache_group` gives it the default `FullAttentionManager` config.
- `SlidingWindowSpec(..., sliding_window=40)` becomes `SlidingWindowManager.layer_config(AttentionSpec(...), sliding_window=40)`. `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks` reads the window from `SlidingWindowManager.Params`.
- `KVCacheGroupSpec(names, spec, enable_kv_transfer=False)` becomes `new_kv_cache_group(names, spec, enable_kv_transfer=False)`.

After this change, nothing in `vllm/` or `tests/` references any of the classes #61452 removed.

Duplicate check: there are no open PRs for `test_umbp_lazy`, `FullAttentionSpec umbp` or `UMBP lazy`, and no later commit on `main` touches this file.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to diagnose the failure, write the change, and run the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Allow min_p and logit_bias with speculative decoding
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stop rejecting `min_p` and `logit_bias` with HTTP 400 when speculative decoding is enabled. Model Runner V2, which runs all in-tree speculative decoding since #63373, already applies both to the target logits before verification, so the request check rejected parameters the sampler can honor.

Fixes #42744.

## Claims

- Requests that set `min_p` or `logit_bias` now succeed with speculative decoding instead of failing with `The min_p and logit_bias sampling parameters are not yet supported with speculative decoding.`
- Both parameters hold on every generated token, including draft tokens accepted during verification. That is the gap #42744 found in Model Runner V1.
- Adds an e2e regression test to the ngram spec-decode suite. Its CI step now also runs when `vllm/sampling_params.py` or the Model Runner V2 sampler (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/`) changes.

## Validation

The new test, `test_ngram_verification_applies_logit_bias_and_min_p`, runs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with ngram drafting (5 speculative tokens). Its main prompt repeats "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.", so drafts copied from the prompt contain ` fox`. With each parameter set, it asserts that drafts are accepted, and:

- Greedy decoding with a `logit_bias` of -100 on ` fox` never emits ` fox`; the unbiased run does.
- At `temperature=1`, `min_p=0.3` never samples a token whose logprob is below `max_logprob + log(min_p)`; the same requests without `min_p` do. This uses the main prompt plus a free-form one.

| Code | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR | passed, 3 of 3 runs |
| Parent commit | failed: `VLLMValidationError: The min_p and logit_bias sampling parameters are not yet supported with speculative decoding.` |
| This PR, logit bias removed from the Model Runner V2 sampler | failed: banned token in the output |
| This PR, `apply_min_p` skipped in the Model Runner V2 sampler | failed: 68 tokens below the `min_p` threshold |

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py::test_ngram_verification_applies_logit_bias_and_min_p
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py  # 64 passed
```

I also checked the OpenAI-compatible server (`vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, 1x A100-80GB). The `min_p` columns use `temperature=1`, and requests were sent concurrently so `min_p` and control requests share batches.

| Speculative decoding | Chat request with `min_p=0.1` or `logit_bias` | `logit_bias` ban and force, T=0 and T=1 (drafts accepted) | Tokens below the `min_p=0.3` threshold | Same, without `min_p` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ngram, 5 tokens, parent commit | 400 | — | — | — |
| ngram, 5 tokens | 200 | pass (440/695) | 0/3072 | 791/1536 |
| EAGLE3, 3 tokens, greedy drafts | 200 | pass (325/750) | 0/3072 | 891/1536 |
| EAGLE3, 3 tokens, probabilistic drafts | 200 | pass (274/900) | 0/3072 | 474/1536 |
| Off | 200 | pass | 0/3072 | 649/1536 |

The EAGLE3 draft model was `jamesliu1/sglang-EAGLE3-Llama-3.1-Instruct-8B`. No accuracy eval: requests that don't set these parameters run the same code as before.

## Details

**Root cause.** The check in `SamplingParams._validate_spec_decode` (added in #31982) reflects a Model Runner V1 limitation. Under speculative decoding, V1's `build_logitsprocs` built only the min-tokens processor and warned "min_p and logit_bias parameters won't work with speculative decoding." #63373 removed Model Runner V1. In Model Runner V2, [`RejectionSampler._verify`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5be8acb7f2e7a9dd22246df3fbbadb173795160e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py#L273-L283) passes the target logits through [`Sampler.apply_sampling_params`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5be8acb7f2e7a9dd22246df3fbbadb173795160e/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py#L252-L265) before `rejection_sample`. That is the same pipeline as non-speculative sampling: logit bias, penalties, bad words, temperature, `min_p`, then top-k/top-p. It's option 1 from #42744 and already in place, so removing the check is the whole fix.

**Compatibility.**
- In-tree, all speculative decoding goes through this rejection sampler: the XPU and CPU runners subclass Model Runner V2, and the standalone CPU runner doesn't support speculative decoding.
- Out-of-tree platforms with their own model runner no longer get this rejection by default. A platform that can't honor these parameters under speculative decoding can reject them in `Platform.validate_request`.
- Don't cherry-pick this onto releases that still ship Model Runner V1 (v0.33.x and earlier). There, the V1 path (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, or configs that fall back to it) would silently drop both parameters.

**Overlapping PRs.**
- #59680 adds a platform opt-out to this same check, so the two PRs conflict. Without the check, that opt-out isn't needed for `min_p` or `logit_bias`. cc @ezietlowTT
- #42802 patches the Model Runner V1 rejection sampler for #42744, but #63373 deleted those files.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel][Quantization] Tensor-descriptor path for int4 fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq (XPU default, sm100 opt-in)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a tensor-descriptor (TD) path to `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` for grouped `int4_w4a16` weights, mirroring the one [#42436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42436) added to `fused_moe_kernel` (RFC [#42545](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42545)). A is gathered with `tensor_descriptor.gather`; packed int4 B is loaded as bytes and unpacked with `tl.interleave`. `int8_w8a16` keeps the pointer path.

## Claims

- **When TD runs:** `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` resolves on (unset: XPU only; `1`: also CUDA sm100+) and the launch reaches the Triton WNA16 kernel. On XPU that needs `--moe-backend triton`, since default serving picks `XPUExpertsWNA16`. sm90 and ROCm always use the pointer path.
- **Fallbacks to the pointer path:**
  - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: TD and pointer may round differently, so all batch sizes stay on one path.
  - `BLOCK_SIZE_M < 8`: the `gather()` minimum.
  - `BLOCK_SIZE_M == 32`: TD is −42% there on Arc Pro B60. Not measured elsewhere, so this applies on every device.
  - A single-token batch, in both GEMMs: the down projection now receives the layer's token count as `num_input_tokens`, because its A has tokens × top_k rows.
  - `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K != 0` (with a one-time warning, like `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`).
  - `BLOCK_SIZE_K < 32`: the packed-byte descriptor needs a 16-byte inner block.
- **Kernel speed:** Arc Pro B60 +13…+17% at M 2–20 and +28…+31% at M 41–4096; Arc Pro B70 +10…+13% at M 4–16 but −4.8% at M 2. Pointer path at M 1 and 21–40.
- **E2E (B70):** prefill-heavy +10–11% for both models and Qwen3-30B mc4 +6.0%. Single-stream decode no longer regresses (+0.8%, was −3.6%). Qwen1.5 mc4 is −1.6% (see Validation). The pointer path matches `main` within 0.7%.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k differences are within the A/A spread. That rules out a drop larger than about 1.5–2 points, not every drop.

## Validation

Unit: `pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "wn16 or wna16"`

| | passed | skipped | failed | tree |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intel Arc Pro B60 (IGC 2.38.2 / compute-runtime 26.27, triton 3.8.0) | 608 | 0 | 0 | this head |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm100) | 480 | 128 (shapes `fused_experts` routes to the CUDA WNA16 kernel) | 0 | this head |
| NVIDIA H200 NVL (sm90, no TD) | 406 | 202 (TD legs) | 0 | this head |

`main` passes the same 384 pre-existing cases on B200 and H200 NVL (CI post-merge image of the base commit).

- `test_fused_moe_wn16`: a `use_td` leg compares TD against the pointer path (tolerance about 6 bf16 ULP at the output magnitude) and the reference. A launch spy asserts which path each GEMM ran.
- `test_triton_wna16_experts_td`: the `--moe-backend triton` route (`TritonWNA16Experts.apply`) with its default config, including BLOCK_SIZE_M 8/16. It asserts no TD in either GEMM for one token.
- `test_fused_moe_wn16_td_forced_config`: forced BLOCK_SIZE_M=8 and an N-tail config.
- `test_wna16_triton_launcher_td_gate`: the fallback decisions, using a fake kernel. On B60, reverting the token gate to launch rows fails its down-projection case and the single-token `test_triton_wna16_experts_td` cases (the spy sees TD in the down projection). Dropping the batch-invariance gate fails its three batch-invariant cases.
- The TD tolerance was widened after a B200 TD-vs-pointer failure at the old one (6.1e-5 abs, 8% rel).
- CI: `test_moe.py` runs in the CUDA MoE kernels job (L4), where the TD legs skip. No CI job runs them on XPU or sm100, so the TD path is covered only by the runs above.

Kernel latency, `fused_experts`, `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-GPTQ-Int4` shapes (E=60, N=1408, K=2048, top-k 4, group 128), default tiles, median of 7 interleaved rounds; positive = TD faster. Pointer-vs-pointer on identical code differs by ≤0.52%.

| tokens M | 1 | 2–20 | 21–40 | 41–4096 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arc Pro B60 | pointer in both GEMMs (−0.1%, noise) | +13…+17% | pointer (TD was −42%) | +28…+31% |
| Arc Pro B70 | pointer in both GEMMs (−0.0%) | M 2: −4.8%, M 3: +8.0%, M 4–16: +10…+13% | not measured | not measured |
| NVIDIA B200, opt-in, `fused_experts` | CUDA WNA16 kernel | CUDA WNA16 kernel | CUDA WNA16 kernel | M ≥ 128: +57…+80% |

On this head B60 M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 measured −0.1%, +13.8%, +12.9%, +14.5%, +13.5%, and its pointer path is within 0.7% of `main` at every M; the other B60 columns are from the previous head, whose dispatch is identical for M > 1. The B70 row is this head. On B200 `fused_experts` sends M·top_k/E ≤ 6 (M ≤ 90 here) to the CUDA WNA16 kernel. `TritonWNA16Experts` sends those shapes to this kernel, where TD runs at BLOCK_SIZE_M 8/16. That regime is unit-tested on B200 but not benchmarked.

E2E: `vllm bench sweep serve`, graph mode, random dataset, seed 42. Arms: `main`, this PR with `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0`, `=1`, and `=0` again (A/A). Each arm-rep runs in a fresh container with a fresh Triton cache, 5 reps interleaved. Output tok/s medians; p is an exact two-sided Mann-Whitney test of TD=1 against both TD=0 arms.

This head, Arc Pro B70. `main` is the 2026-10-26 XPU nightly (`00b6c4c565`); the PR arms add this PR's four runtime files to it (same patch as this head).

| model | scenario (in/out tokens, prompts, concurrency) | TD=1 vs TD=0 | A/A | p | TPOT ms TD=0 → TD=1 | PR TD=0 vs `main` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | batch1 (1024/512, 10, c1) | +0.8% | −0.1% | 0.0007 | 9.22 → 9.22 | −0.0% |
| Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | mc4 (1024/1024, 20, c4) | **−1.6%** | −0.1% | 0.0007 | 14.25 → 14.56 | +0.1% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | batch1 | +0.8% | −0.1% | 0.0007 | 14.23 → 14.23 | −0.1% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | mc4 | +6.0% | −0.8% | 0.028 | 18.52 → 17.51 | −0.7% |

- A dispatch probe at graph capture shows both GEMMs on the pointer path for batch size 1 and TD from batch size 2. On the previous head the down projection ran TD at batch size 1, which caused its batch1 −3.6%.
- Qwen1.5 mc4 decodes mostly at 4 tokens, where the B70 kernel benchmark has TD 10.5% faster. The cause of the E2E slowdown is not established.

Previous head `a0b1f2262a`, TD=1 vs TD=0, other scenarios (identical dispatch except single-token steps):

| scenario (in/out tokens, prompts, concurrency) | B70 Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | B70 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | B200 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy (4000/200, 30) | +10.4% (A/A +0.3) | +11.4% (A/A +0.8) | +235% (A/A +0.1) |
| decode_heavy (200/2000, 10) | +0.8% (A/A −2.3) | +0.7% (A/A +3.9) | +161% (A/A +5.4) |
| mixed (1024/1024, 20) | +1.8% (A/A −1.2) | +0.7% (A/A +3.5) | +188% (A/A −5.4) |
| mid32 (200/1000, 32, c32) | +1.3% (A/A −0.3) | +0.2% (A/A +1.8) | +179% (A/A −0.0) |
| mc4 | — | — | +1.5% (A/A +0.6) |
| batch1 | — | — | +2.5% (A/A −0.1) |

- The B200 baseline is the Triton pointer path, which `--moe-backend triton` selects. Default CUDA serving does not use it.
- Engine args: `--moe-backend triton --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192`; Qwen1.5 also `--quantization moe_wna16`.
- Attention was Flash Attention in every logged run (dispatch probe and gsm8k; perf server logs were not kept), so the flag did not toggle Triton-attention TD.
- Qwen1.5 GPTQ produces garbage on CUDA in every arm, including pristine `main`, so it has no B200 column.

gsm8k, `lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, full test set, flexible extract, previous head:

| | TD=0 | TD=1 | TD=0 repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| B70 Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | 0.4602 | 0.4716 | 0.4655 |
| B70 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | 0.8772 | 0.8711 | 0.8696 |
| B200 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | 0.8848 | 0.8802 | 0.8795 |

The B200 first TD=0 arm differs from both later arms (98.9% identical generations between the repeat and TD=1, 45.9% against the first). It ran first, so treat it as a run-order outlier.

All XPU E2E and accuracy runs used IGC 2.34.4 / compute-runtime 26.18. The `main` stack (IGC 2.38.2 / compute-runtime 26.27) crashes int4 Triton MoE at model level, with and without TD (checked on an earlier tree, not on this head). Unit tests ran on 26.27.

## Details

- **Overlap with [#52577](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52577):**
  - #52577 masks the pointer-path B load, which this PR moves under `else:`. The conflict is textual.
  - The `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K` fallback routes ragged-K launches onto that same unmasked load, so #52577 should land first. Whichever lands second keeps its mask.
- **Other open PRs on this launch site:**
  - [#56154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56154) rewrites it into a warmup dispatcher.
  - [#56788](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56788) and [#57558](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57558) add tuned XPU configs, which use BLOCK_SIZE_M=32 for some shapes. Those launches would stay on the pointer path.
  - No open PR adds TD to this kernel.
- **Allocator:** `set_triton_allocator` is registered as in `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`. [#61583](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61583) reports that XPU never calls it and that registering it can break torch.compile `split_module`. The graph-mode E2E runs above did not hit that.
- **Design:**
  - The B descriptor is built inside the kernel, as in `fused_moe_kernel`'s TD path.
  - [#63820](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63820) builds a host `TensorDescriptor` for fp8 B on sm90 (`USE_TMA_B`), which ignores `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`. A host descriptor for packed int4 B was not tried.
- **Default on XPU:** RFC #42545 asks for a separate PR to flip a kernel's default. Like #42436, this PR converts the kernel and follows the shared XPU default in one step; `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0` turns it off. Its `envs.py` entry now lists every consumer.
- **Not covered:** TP > 1, EP, int8, AWQ and Quark checkpoints.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Bump DeepGEMM for the MegaMoE combine-readiness fix under CUDA graph replay
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bump DeepGEMM to vllm-project/DeepGEMM@196f338, which adds vllm-project/DeepGEMM#59: a cherry-pick of deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#451, extended to the SiTU and NVFP4 kernels. It fixes stale MegaMoE outputs under CUDA graph replay at EP > 1. It is the only commit between the current pin (`0f7698f`) and the new one.

## Claims

- DeepGEMM MegaMoE (`--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`) no longer combines a previous replay's data when its CUDA graphs are replayed with more than one EP rank. This affects the SM100 FP8×FP4 (SwiGLU and SiTU), BF16 and NVFP4 kernels.
- No vLLM code changes, and no kernel performance change is expected.

## Validation

**Reproducer, in DeepGEMM's own test** (4x GB200, EP4). The test compares CUDA graph replays bitwise against eager launches with alternating inputs:

```
python tests/test_mega_moe.py --num-processes 4 --num-max-tokens-per-rank 1000 --num-tokens 1000 \
  --hidden 2560 --intermediate-hidden 640 --num-experts 256 --num-topk 8 --num-shared-experts 0 \
  --emu-reference --num-correctness-tests 1
```

| DeepGEMM | Accuracy vs PyTorch reference | CUDA graph replay vs eager |
|---|---|---|
| `0f7698f` (current pin) | pass | fails, 2/2 runs: `CUDA graph replay 2 differs from the eager launch` |
| `196f338` (this PR) | pass | passes, 2/2 runs |

**vLLM, with the vendored DeepGEMM built at the new pin** (`cmake --build ... --target _deep_gemm_C`, GB200): `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` gives 146 passed, 1 skipped.

**CI:** this test needs multiple SM100 GPUs, and vLLM's DeepGEMM MegaMoE tests do not replay CUDA graphs across EP ranks, so CI does not cover it. The validation above was run outside CI.

## Details

**Root cause.** MegaMoE tags combine readiness with the launch's `%gridid` (`grid index + 1`). A CUDA graph kernel node keeps the same `%gridid` on every replay, so a rank could accept a peer's readiness tag left over from the previous replay. It would then read that peer's combine data before the current launch's L2 writes landed.

**Fix (in DeepGEMM).** Before the existing dispatch pull barrier, each rank clears its local readiness flags. The barrier orders that reset before every peer's current completion notification. There is no new barrier and no workspace or ABI change.

This is the MegaMoE counterpart of the `mega_mhc` graph-replay fix that is already pinned (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#48, a cherry-pick of deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#478).

**Duplicates.** No open vLLM PR bumps this pin or fixes this issue: I searched open PRs for DeepGEMM pin bumps and MegaMoE graph replay.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Retry the CUDA image bake when the registry rate-limits the push
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The CUDA `:docker: Build image` step (`image-build`) compiles for about 1.5 h and then pushes `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-test-repo:<commit>` from inside `docker buildx bake` (`output = ["type=registry"]` in ci-infra's `docker/ci.hcl`). When public ECR throttles that push, the bake fails:

```
#121 exporting to image
#121 pushing layers 0.2s done
#121 ERROR: failed to push public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-test-repo:d43226c5...: toomanyrequests: Rate exceeded
...
ERROR: failed to solve: failed to push public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-test-repo:d43226c5...: toomanyrequests: Rate exceeded
🚨 Error: The command exited with status 1
```

The step's `retry.automatic` only covers agent-lost exits (-1, -10), so each of these failures needed a manual retry, and every GPU job in the build waited for it. From 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-10 this happened 19 times, costing about 55 CPU-hours. The failures came in bursts: 14 builds were throttled within the same 10 s on 2026-11-10 16:24Z, and 5 within 20 s on 2026-11-06 01:46Z. Base-image pulls were not affected, and the private ECR cache import/export was not either. The cache export was only canceled when the image push failed.

Example logs:
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100384#01a1ae66-943e-4521-a646-ded6c3a991c9
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101459#01a1c52f-15c6-487d-a804-6a1429b74684
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101493#01a1c5e7-878a-4f67-821e-83cd038c9455
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101499#01a1c605-9f2c-4ca9-9922-b5a8fedfbe85

## Change

`.buildkite/image_build/image_build.sh` now runs the main bake through `bake_with_rate_limit_retry`:

- The bake output is copied to a log file in `BUILD_TMP_DIR` and still streams to the job log.
- If the bake fails **and** BuildKit's final error line (`^ERROR: ... failed to solve: ...`) contains `toomanyrequests` or `too many requests`, the script waits and reruns the same bake command. The wait is exponential backoff plus jitter: `60·2^(n-1) + rand(0..60)` s, which gives 60–120, 120–180 and 240–300 s. The jitter matters because the throttling hits many builds at once.
- There are at most 4 attempts, so the extra wait is at most about 10 min. Both knobs can be set through `IMAGE_BUILD_RATE_LIMIT_ATTEMPTS` and `IMAGE_BUILD_RATE_LIMIT_BASE_DELAY`.
- Every other failure is returned unchanged on the first attempt. That includes compile and `RUN` step failures, and a 429 printed by a `RUN` step.

**Why a rerun doesn't recompile:** the rerun uses the same builder in the same job. That builder is either the local `buildkitd` via the remote driver or the `docker-container` builder. Its local cache still holds every layer that just finished, so the second bake is all cache hits: it re-exports the image (about 40 s) and retries the push and the cache export. Re-resolving the cached steps also covers a throttled base-image pull (`429 Too Many Requests` on resolve). That case costs little anyway because it fails early.

**Alternative considered:** a Buildkite `retry: automatic` rule on exit status 1 in `image_build.yaml`. Exit 1 is what every real compile failure returns too, so the rule would also retry broken builds. A Buildkite retry also lands on a fresh agent, possibly a different instance. There it would rebuild from the registry cache, and the CUDA cache layers for this commit may not have been exported, because the cache export is canceled when the push fails. In the worst case that means repeating the 1.5 h compile. Retrying inside the job avoids both problems.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR addresses this. I searched `gh pr list -R vllm-project/vllm` for "toomanyrequests", "rate exceeded" + image_build, and "image push retry".

**Out of scope / follow-ups:**
- The other image scripts (`image_build_cpu.sh`, `_xpu`, `_arm64`, `_torch_nightly`) push with their own commands and are not changed here.
- The bursts suggest the account hits a public ECR push TPS limit when many builds finish together. Pushing CI-only images to the private ECR registry, which is already used for the cache, would remove the dependency on public ECR rate limits altogether. That change would belong in ci-infra (`docker/ci.hcl`, `REGISTRY`/`REPO`).

## Test Plan

- `shellcheck -s bash --format=gcc --rcfile=tools/pre_commit/.shellcheckrc .buildkite/image_build/image_build.sh` (v0.11.0, same as the pre-commit hook) and `bash -n`.
- A local harness that extracts `is_registry_rate_limited` and `bake_with_rate_limit_retry` from the script and drives them with a fake bake, with `sleep` stubbed out.
- The matcher run against the downloaded CI logs:
  - all 19 real rate-limited image-build logs (Buildkite timestamp prefix stripped);
  - 5 non-rate-limit image-build failures: an `apt-get` exit 100, `flashinfer download-kernels`, the DeepEP build and a canceled job.

## Test Result

- shellcheck: clean. `bash -n`: OK.
- Harness: all 7 cases pass.

  | Case | Bake calls | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | Success on the first try | 1 | exit 0 |
  | Push `toomanyrequests`, then OK | 2 | exit 0 |
  | Pull `429 Too Many Requests` twice, then OK | 3 | exit 0 |
  | Rate limit that never clears | 4 | exit 1 |
  | Compile failure | 1 | exit 1, no retry |
  | `RUN`-step 429 | 1 | exit 1, no retry |
  | `IMAGE_BUILD_RATE_LIMIT_ATTEMPTS=1` | 1 | exit 1, retry disabled |

- Real logs: 19/19 rate-limited logs matched, and 0/5 other failures matched.
- Not yet exercised end to end on a CI agent: that needs a real throttle event.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Keep the mock engine alive in the test_app fixture
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm-server`'s `routes::tests::request_id_header_is_absent_by_default` fails intermittently on `main` with `/health` returning 503 instead of 200, mostly in full-workspace `cargo nextest` runs. The `test_app()` fixture drops its mock engine before handing out the router, and since vllm-project/vllm#67187 the client notices the disconnected engine. This PR keeps the mock engine alive for as long as the test holds the router.

## Claims

- `test_app()` and `test_app_with_dev_mode()` return the mock engine task together with the router, like the other app fixtures (`test_app_with_request_id_headers`, `test_app_with_api_keys`, `test_app_with_cors`, ...). The 36 tests built on them hold it as `_engine_task`.
- `request_id_header_is_absent_by_default` no longer races with the engine shutdown. Test code only; no production change.

## Validation

Making the race deterministic: a 200 ms sleep inserted between `test_app()` and the `/health` request in `request_id_header_is_absent_by_default` (local probe, not committed):

| Base | Result |
|---|---|
| `0fab1aa459~1` (before vllm-project/vllm#67187) | pass |
| `main` `ab72c466aa` | 503, every run |
| this PR | pass, 3 of 3 runs |

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `ab72c466aa`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 5 consecutive runs: 2685 passed, 13 skipped each
```

Without this change, three full-workspace runs on the same machine (one on `main`, two on a branch that does not touch `vllm-server`) each failed this test with the 503.

## Details

**Root cause.** `test_app_with_dev_mode` bound the `MockEngineTask` from `test_models_with_engine_outputs_and_backend` to a local and returned only the router, so the task was dropped on return, and its `Drop` aborts the mock engine. None of the 36 tests on this fixture submits to the engine: they cover unimplemented routes, `/v1/models`, `/version`, `/server_info`, `/tokenize` and `/detokenize`, metrics, and request validation errors returned before submission. So the dead engine went unnoticed until vllm-project/vllm#67187 added `run_input_watch_loop`, which turns a `Disconnected` event on the input socket into `EngineDisconnected`. `/health` is the only one of these routes that reads engine liveness, so it returns 503 whenever the event arrives before the request.

**Fix.** The production behavior is correct: a disconnected engine should make `/health` fail. The bug is the fixture handing out a router whose engine it already shut down, so the fix returns the engine task with the router. A scan of `rust/` found no other fixture that creates a mock engine and drops it before returning.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this fixture or the test.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

## Overview

Move `CMakeLists.txt` from `run_all_patterns` to `amd_run_all_patterns` in `.buildkite/ci_config.yaml`, as #65762 did for `csrc/`. ci-selector then decides `CMakeLists.txt` edits on CUDA, and AMD still runs everything.

**Merge after vllm-project/ci-infra#895 and vllm-project/ci-infra#891.**

## Claims

- A `CMakeLists.txt` edit no longer runs every CUDA step. It runs the steps for the `csrc/` sources it compiles, which the kernel record narrows further.
- AMD behaves as before: a `CMakeLists.txt` edit still runs every non-optional AMD step.
- Anything the selector's CMake walk cannot follow (global flags, `include()`, extension-target arguments, unknown commands) still runs everything.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Keep dynamic speculative decoding for dense models with DP
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Dynamic speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`) is no longer disabled for dense models with data parallelism; it stays disabled only for MoE models, whose DP ranks step in lockstep. Follows up on #45963, which added the DP gate.

## Claims

- With `--data-parallel-size > 1`, a dense model keeps its dynamic speculative-token schedule on every DP rank instead of falling back to the static `num_speculative_tokens`.
- MoE models with DP are unchanged: the schedule is still disabled with the same warning.
- Docs updated: `docs/features/speculative_decoding/dynamic_speculative_decoding.md`.

## Validation

Tests: `test_dynamic_sd_with_data_parallel[dense|moe]` in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py` (replaces `test_dynamic_sd_is_disabled_with_data_parallel`), and `test_dense_dp_ranks_follow_dynamic_sd_schedule` in `tests/v1/distributed/test_dense_dp_world_size.py` (`RemoteOpenAIServer`, DP from `DP_SIZE`, `draft_model` on `vllm-project/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` with a schedule that drafts 0 tokens at every batch size and a static K of 3; asserts `vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total` stays 0). The test starts its own server, like the other tests in that module, so it never shares GPUs with another server.

```
pytest -v -s tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py -k with_data_parallel
DP_SIZE=2 TP_SIZE=1 pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_dense_dp_world_size.py -k dynamic_sd
```

| Test | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_dynamic_sd_with_data_parallel[dense]` | FAILED: `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size` is `None` | PASSED |
| `test_dynamic_sd_with_data_parallel[moe]` | PASSED (schedule disabled) | PASSED (schedule disabled) |
| e2e dynamic SD test (DP=2) | FAILED: 84 draft tokens (`engine="0"`: 42, `engine="1"`: 42), i.e. static K=3 | PASSED: 0 draft tokens |
| Full `test_dynamic_sd.py` | | 18 passed |

These ran on x86_64 CPU (no GPU used): vLLM's CPU nightly wheel for f5d93296c8 with this PR's `vllm/config/vllm.py` swapped in; between that commit and this PR's base, `vllm/config/`, `vllm/v1/core/sched/`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/`, `vllm/v1/engine/` and the touched tests are identical. The e2e results above were measured with the same test body in `test_multi_api_servers.py` (plus `--api-server-count 4`), before it moved to `test_dense_dp_world_size.py` when main was merged in; it also passed there with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`. In CI, the unit tests run in "Spec Decode" and the e2e test in "Distributed DP Extended" (`DP_SIZE=4`) and the Rust frontend distributed step. `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

## Details

#45963 disables the schedule whenever `data_parallel_size > 1` because each rank picks K from its own batch, and the drafter's DP collectives then diverge between ranks. That only applies when DP ranks run together, which is the MoE case (`DPEngineCoreProc`). For a dense model, `run_engine_core` calls `parallel_config.reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` and starts a plain `EngineCoreProc`, so each rank runs with `data_parallel_size == 1` and has no DP collectives. But the gate runs in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` in the API server, before that reconfiguration, so it also disabled the schedule for dense models.

The new condition keeps the gate when `model_config` is missing or the model is MoE. The existing DP test asserted the warning text, which is logged with `warning_once`, so it depended on test order; the rewritten test asserts the schedule and the scheduled K instead.

Related: draft #66671 adds `--independent-data-parallel` for MoE and lifts the same gate when that flag is set. The two compose: with both, the gate would apply only to MoE ranks in lockstep.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Keep the fused gated RMSNorm for the KDA o_norm
commits.pr_body:
GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA output norm runs on ROCm as a chain of eager elementwise kernels instead of one fused launch, because the model runs in `VLLM_COMPILE` mode with custom ops off but has no `@support_torch_compile` region that would let Inductor fuse `forward_native`; this PR makes `Glm5NextLinearAttention` keep the fused `rms_norm_gated` kernel on ROCm through `CustomOp`'s `enforce_enable`; other platforms keep following `custom_ops`.

On ROCm `Glm5Next*` is not a default breakable-CUDA-graph architecture, so it gets `custom_ops=["none"]` and all 34 KDA layers' `o_norm` (`FusedRMSNormGated`) run `forward_native`, in the FULL decode graphs and in prefill. `FusedRMSNormGated` now forwards `enforce_enable` to `CustomOp.__init__` (default `False`: `bailing_moe_v3`, `kimi_gdn_linear_attn`, Kimi-K3 unchanged). CUDA already takes `forward_cuda` (by source). Only `glm5_next` builds this layer.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Tests and `o_norm` timings on `main@b0fd6874a0` (vLLM `083fbac02`, AITER 0.1.28.post1); rebased onto `960f5c1bb1`, `o_norm` path unchanged.

**Tests.** `test_kda_o_norm.py` (a real KDA layer under `VLLM_COMPILE` + `custom_ops=["none"]` runs the fused kernel on ROCm and `forward_native` elsewhere) and `test_fused_rms_norm_gated.py::test_enforce_enable_with_custom_ops_off`: 13 pass; on `main` 5 fail, with `enforce_enable` not forwarded 3, without the GLM layer setting it 1. In a live engine all 34 `o_norm` switch to `forward_hip`.

**`o_norm`, us/call**, `main` → PR, median of runs 2-4 of 4 (`head_dim=128`, bf16; graph = 20 captured calls replayed as in decode, eager = back-to-back as in prefill): all 12 graph shapes −89 to −92%, all 6 eager −66 to −88%. Heads×tokens, graph: 64×1 20.46 → 2.18, 64×64 27.69 → 2.45, 64×256 45.41 → 4.29, 32×64 TP2 23.81 → 2.34; eager: 64×509 68.46 → 23.39, 64×2047 191.08 → 23.45. Spread ≤ 2.9 us graph, 8.3 us eager.

**Serving, by hand** (2026-11-11): `main` `a58e84c8cb` (Python on the image's compiled extensions) vs + this PR's diff. Fresh `vllm serve --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` per run; random 1000/600 unless stated, 32-512 prompts; arms alternate, 4 runs each, first dropped, median of runs 2-4 [min-max]; every range is disjoint.

|1|16|2194 [2160-2201]|2315 [2278-2319]|+5.5%|
|1|64|4827 [4812-4841]|5039 [5034-5052]|+4.4%|

|1|16, 4000/200|9700 [9642-9710]|10318 [10234-10339]|+6.4%|
|1|64, 200/1000|2520 [2507-2531]|2614 [2602-2630]|+3.7%|

|2|64|7126 [7122-7126]|7520 [7516-7533]|+5.5%|
|2|128|9581 [9572-9606]|9988 [9971-10035]|+4.3%|
|4|16|3987 [3967-3996]|4379 [4375-4391]|+9.8%|

Every config gains outside the noise and mean TPOT falls 3.1-10.2% (all disjoint): each decode step's 34 `o_norm` run fused in the FULL graphs. Earlier automated run (TP1 conc 50, `b0fd6874a0`): +3.1%, Kimi-Linear-48B control −0.25%.

**Accuracy: no difference outside run-to-run noise.** `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 items, `max_gen_toks=256`, strict-match, `main` → PR: MXFP4 TP1, 7 runs each, 0.9239 → 0.9200 (−0.0039, Welch p 0.16; the first 3 per arm read −0.0071, and an earlier 4 vs 3 on `b0fd6874a0` −0.0072); 2 runs each: MXFP4 TP2 0.9155 → 0.9200, the fp8 checkpoint at TP2 0.9158 → 0.9181, the BF16 checkpoint at TP4 0.9299 → 0.9318. GPQA Diamond CoT (flexible-extract), MXFP4 TP1, 4 runs each: 0.5290 → 0.5227 (−0.0063; one question is 0.005; p 0.75). ## Overview

Give `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe` and `test_online_quantize_reload` the reload headroom that #56492 gave `test_reload_weights`. Both predate #56492 and OOM on main since. Reported on #54477 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477#issuecomment-6819419244)).

## Claims

- Both tests pass again on CUDA. Test-only, 4 lines.

## Validation

Main `94febce` ± this change:

| | 1x L40S | 1x L4 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 2 failed (OOM) | 2 failed (OOM) |
| this PR, two runs | 2 passed, 2 passed | lora_moe passes; DeepSeek-V3 still OOMs |
| `test_reload.py -m "(not slow_test) and (not distributed)"` | 82 passed, 1 skipped | 82 passed, 1 skipped |

<details>
<summary>L40S output</summary>

main:

```
Updating weights layer by layer needs about 3.94 GiB of free device memory, at least 1.31 GiB for the largest layer alone, but only 1.46 GiB is free ...
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 448.00 MiB. ...
Updating weights layer by layer needs about 1.74 GiB of free device memory, at least 0.58 GiB for the largest layer alone, but only 1.05 GiB is free ...
```
