commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 native linear: 256x256x128 tile for large prefill GEMMs on gfx950
commits.pr_body:
On gfx950, large-K MXFP8 prefill GEMMs with M > 1024 run on a `128x128x256` tile, which reloads the activation, weight and E8M0 scale tiles for every 128x128 of output; this adds a `256x256x128` tile (4 warps, 2 stages) to `_select_cfg` that reuses each load over 4x the output area, taken when N > 1024 and the 128x128 grid needs at least 10/3 as many CU waves as the 256x256 grid.

Unchanged: M, K or N <= 1024, `_M31_TILES` rows, other targets, DeepSeek-V4.1's 32x32-block path. All 240 attention, dense and shared-expert linears of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 reach `_select_cfg`; a 15k-token prefill hit six shapes at M = 15015/16384, all on the new tile. MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 has the same linears (not run). Also fixes a `TypeError` in `benchmark_mxfp8_tp4.py` and adds `--shape-set prefill`.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950, 256 CUs). Kernel, GSM8K and tests on `main` `ceb319b5` (torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0).

**Kernel.** HIP-graph replay, >= 400 MiB rotating weights, median of 30 device-event samples, 4 fresh processes per arm, median of runs 2-4, spread <= 0.66%. Of 59 TP1/2/4 prefill shapes, the 39 whose tile changes gain a median +28.9% (+7.2% to +46.5%), the other 20 -0.16% to +0.48%; output bit-identical on all 59.

|linear (N, K), M|waves 128/256|`main` µs|PR µs|Δ|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|TP1 qkv (9856, 6144), 16384|39/10|1572.6|1137.0|+38.3%|
|same, 4096|10/3|359.7|335.5|+7.2%|
|same, 2048 (old tile)|5/2|183.0|182.7|+0.2%|
|TP1 gate_up (24576, 6144), 16384|96/24|3855.5|2727.6|+41.4%|
|TP1 shared down (6144, 3072), 16384|24/6|526.2|359.2|+46.5%|
|TP1 down (6144, 12288), 9349|14/4|1088.2|934.6|+16.4%|
|TP4 qkv (2560, 6144), 16380|10/3|399.0|341.6|+16.8%|

**Serving**, by hand, 2026-11-11: `main` `3ec1b24a` (Python on the image's compiled extensions) vs + this PR's diff; fresh `vllm serve --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92` per run; random 3900/150 unless stated, 64-512 prompts; arms alternate, 4 runs each, first dropped, median of runs 2-4 [min-max]; unmarked rows: disjoint ranges. TP4 = recipe TP.

|TP|conc|`main` tok/s|PR|Δ|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|1|1|2871 [2849-2885]|2878 [2868-2887]|+0.2% overlap|
|1|16|12247 [12234-12319]|12607 [12576-12707]|+2.9%|
|1|64|16866 [16821-16903]|17619 [17473-17829]|+4.5%|
|1|16, 1024/1024|1696 [1689-1728]|1705 [1691-1742]|+0.5% overlap|
|2|16|12726 [12721-12736]|12932 [12455-12962]|+1.6% overlap|
|2|64|16224 [16051-16237]|16679 [16618-16685]|+2.8%|
|4|16|20378 [19560-20385]|20567 [20316-20593]|+0.9% overlap|
|4|64|26999 [26981-27000]|27349 [27326-27363]|+1.3%|
|4|128|29502 [29448-29582]|29918 [29904-29925]|+1.4%|

In unmarked rows mean TTFT falls 0.3-9.5%, TPOT 0.4-3.7%. The gain falls with TP because per-rank GEMMs shrink, so fewer prefill GEMMs cross the wave gate; at conc 1 prompts prefill one at a time and M = 1 decode (~85% of the run) never takes the tile: nothing changes. Earlier automated TP1 conc 16 run: +3.9%; Llama-3.1-8B control (no MXFP8 linear) -0.2%.

**GSM8K** (TP1, 5-shot, chat template, greedy, 1319 items, `max_gen_toks=1024`, one run per arm), strict-match: `main` 0.9500 ± 0.0060, this PR 0.9545 ± 0.0057, `main` again 0.9439 ± 0.0063.

**Tests.** `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` pins the gate on 18 `(M, N, K, CUs)` cases and its gfx950 guard, and checks the tile against the dequantized reference on the six TP1 linears. Wrong versions (no gfx950 or N > 1024 guard, fixed M/N bounds, fixed 3 waves, hard-coded CUs, before the short-K bucket) each fail a case. 268 pass on MI355X; on `main` only the 15 new cases fail.

## Details

Whole waves (a partial wave costs a full one): over 167 swept points the tile wins 0/3 below a wave ratio of 3 (median -18.4%), 24/51 at 3 (-0.3%), 18/20 at 3–3.25 (+10.8%), 93/93 from 10/3 (+19.9%, min +0.4%). A fixed `cdiv(M, 256) * cdiv(N, 256) >= 3 * CUs` would admit M=5041, N=9856 (-3.6%) and miss the TP4 qkv at M=16380.

Related: #66330 (`128x128x128`, grouped launch) edits this branch: +8.1% median on these shapes alone (-13.5% at M=2048, TP1), +32.5% behind this gate; whichever lands second keeps this tile first. #65479 / #64089 move AITER-tuned (N, K), today the TP4 linears, to AITER; #66600 (M <= 16) composes.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find, measure and write this change; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [XPU][Kimi-K3] Run KDA metadata tests on XPU
commits.pr_body:
The Kimi-K3 KDA metadata builder only launches Triton kernels, but its tests were gated on torch.cuda.is_available() with a hard-coded "cuda" device, and the kernel wrappers asserted tensor.is_cuda. On XPU this skipped 20 cases that pass there.

Gate the tests on a CUDA-alike or XPU device, use the platform device type, and check the device type against current_platform in the wrappers.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Build AITER MLA full-graph decode metadata in one kernel
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Under full CUDA graphs, `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._build_decode` fills the persistent decode metadata buffers (`graph_seq_lens`, `paged_kv_indptr`, `qo_indptr`, and for adaptive verification the varlen q/o row maps) with 10-25 small eager ops per build. This PR does it in a single Triton kernel, `_build_decode_indptr_kernel`, on the non-DCP full-graph decode path.

No open PR covers this: #65022 (split metadata lifetime) and #64560 (decode q absorb/quant fusion) touch the same backend but not this metadata build; #61504 / #58352 target the sparse MLA backend.

## Claims

Kimi-K3 official recipe (TP8, DSpark MTP 7 tokens, fp8 KV, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), MI355X, per decode metadata build:

| Mode | Kernels | GPU time | Host time (p50) |
|---|---|---|---|
| uniform MTP (recipe default) | 11 → 4 | 60.2 → 40.6 µs (-33%) | 211 → 158 µs (-25%) |
| adaptive verification (varlen) | 24.5 → 4.7 | 134.7 → 48.4 µs (-64%) | 342 → 163 µs (-52%) |

- The fused kernel's outputs (kernel KV lengths, both indptrs, varlen row maps) are bit-identical to the eager build's (the only difference is the never-read dump slot of the varlen o-row map).
- No new host/device synchronization.
- DCP (`dcp_world_size > 1`) keeps the existing eager path unchanged.
- Faster than the eager ops at every `max_num_seqs` up to 1024 and every batch size (microbenchmark below); end to end, decode steps are 0.2-0.56% faster at concurrency 1-8 and unchanged within noise at 16-64.

## Validation

All runs on one MI355X node (8 GPUs), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` at `e0d00e4b`; `rocm_aiter_mla.py` and `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` are unchanged on main since then.

**Unit tests** (8 GPUs, `main` vs this PR):

```
pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py tests/v1/attention/test_expand_page_indices.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_aiter_mla_uniform_mtp_qo_len.py "tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_*.py" \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py \
  "tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_*.py"
```

| | passed | skipped | failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 963 | 6 | 1 (`test_rocm_aiter_mla_prefill_fusions.py::test_fused_prefill_context_matches_unfused[context_lens1-2]`, intermittent on main, unrelated) |
| this PR | 989 | 6 | 0 |

The new builder tests run the real `_build_decode` with and without the fused path and compare the metadata and graph buffers (tails included) for uniform / varlen / non-padded decode, with 8-, 64- and 1024-request buffers at batch 1, half and full. They also assert that DCP batches never launch the fused kernel and that an oversized batch is rejected. MTP widths 1, 3, 4 and 7 are covered (uniform with a dummy row, mixed lengths, and mixed lengths under adaptive verification); these cases were added after the run above, and `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` alone gives 107 passed, 0 failed. Because that module skips off ROCm, `test_aiter_mla_decode_indptr_kernel.py` also checks the kernel directly against the eager build on any GPU (no AITER needed), so the required NVIDIA V1 Attention steps run it too: 33 passed on MI355X.

**Kernel cost vs `max_num_seqs`** (MI355X, one GPU, 8 query tokens per request, GPU time = sum of kernel durations per build from torch profiler):

| Mode | `max_num_seqs` | batch 1: eager → fused | half: eager → fused | full: eager → fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform | 8 / 64 / 256 / 512 | 25 → 2.0 µs | 25 → 2.0 µs | 21-23 → 2.0 µs |
| uniform | 1024 | 26 → 2.3 µs | 27 → 2.5 µs | 24 → 2.8 µs |
| adaptive | 8 / 64 | 61 → 2.0 µs | 59 → 2.1 µs | 56 → 2.1 µs |
| adaptive | 256 | 63 → 3.6 µs | 64 → 3.6 µs | 67 → 3.7 µs |
| adaptive | 512 | 64 → 5.0 µs | 70 → 5.1 µs | 71 → 5.2 µs |
| adaptive | 1024 | 66 → 8.1 µs | 76 → 8.2 µs | 78 → 8.5 µs |

The single program is sized by `max_num_seqs`, so its cost grows with the buffer rather than the live batch, but it stays 8-30x cheaper than the eager ops everywhere. Host launch time is ~17 µs fused vs 77-213 µs eager, independent of `max_num_seqs`. (The eager reference here rebuilds its row ids each call, so its varlen kernel count is slightly higher than in the builder.)

**Serving correctness** (Kimi-K3 recipe, gsm8k 5-shot, full 1319 questions, greedy). A shadow check also re-verified after every build that all page indices past the live pages are -1 (uniform/adaptive: thousands to 16k builds per rank, 0 mismatches).

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| uniform | 94.92% | 95.38% |
| adaptive | 94.92% | 95.83% |
| DCP=8 / DCP=8 + adaptive (first 400 questions) | - | 98.5% / 98.25% (fused path not taken, as expected) |

**NIAH** (Kimi-K3 recipe, RULER `niah_single_2`, first 100 items per length, greedy, `max_tokens` 128, paired per item, main vs this PR; a hit means the needle value appears in the answer):

| Length | Items | main | this PR | main only | PR only |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32k | 100 | 100% | 100% | 0 | 0 |
| 64k | 100 | 100% | 100% | 0 | 0 |
| 128k | 100 | 100% | 100% | 0 | 0 |

**GPQA Diamond** (Kimi-K3 recipe, 198 questions, simple-evals prompt, answer regex and option shuffle, greedy, `max_tokens` 32768, two runs per side):

| Run | main | this PR | main only | PR only | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 91.9% | 86.9% | 12 | 2 | 0.013 |
| 2 | 90.4% | 90.9% | 5 | 6 | 1.0 |
| pooled (396) | 91.2% | 88.9% | | | |

Run 1 alone looked like a regression, so run 2 added a shadow check to this PR's side: after every fused build it recomputed the eager reference (kernel lengths, both indptrs with their tails, the page-index tail, the varlen row maps) and compared all of them. Across 1,394,688 fused builds over the whole run there were 0 mismatches, so the metadata the attention kernels read was identical to main's. The check itself was validated first on the builder tests (0 mismatches clean; every fused build flagged when one entry is corrupted on purpose). The GPQA numbers alone do not establish equivalence: the pooled difference is -2.3 points with a 95% bootstrap interval of [-5.1, +0.3] over questions, and that interval treats questions as independent, which understates run-level variation (the same PR code moved from 86.9% to 90.9% between runs, 1 vs 9 discordant, p = 0.021; main moved from 91.9% to 90.4%). Serving is not reproducible here even for main alone: 0 of 198 responses were identical between main's two runs. A follow-up check removed the obvious sources of run-to-run variation (concurrency 1, prefix caching off, a fixed per-request seed, temperature 0) and restarted the main server between two passes over the first 10 questions: still 0 of 10 identical with DSpark and 0 of 10 identical without speculative decoding, with responses diverging within the first 16 to 564 characters. Token-level comparison against main is therefore not possible on this stack, and per-run accuracy differences on long generations are a property of the serving stack rather than evidence about this PR. The evidence that this PR does not change what the model computes is the bit-identical attention metadata (here and in the two serving runs below), not the accuracy numbers.

GPQA with the recipe only exercises the kernel's uniform-MTP branch, so the same shadow check was run on two more servers (GPQA prompts as load, `max_tokens` 2048) to cover the other two branches in serving:

| Server | Fused builds checked | Mismatches |
|---|---|---|
| adaptive verification (`enable_adaptive_verification`, max-num-seqs 8) | 331,776 (221,184 varlen, 110,592 plain) | 0 |
| no speculative decoding (1-token decode, max-num-seqs 64, batches up to 64) | 49,152 (plain) | 0 |

**End-to-end** (decode step period p50, main vs this PR, ABBA interleaved, server restarted per leg, 512 output tokens per request, 8 × concurrency requests per window). The step period is used instead of TPOT because DSpark acceptance length varies by ±8% across runs, which swamps TPOT and throughput at this effect size.

| Config | Concurrency | Step period | Change | Pairs | Paired t |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| recipe (`--max-num-seqs 8`) | 1 | ~18.0 ms | -0.20% | 4 | -1.4 |
| | 4 | ~23.8 ms | -0.44% | 4 | -2.7 |
| | 8 | ~28.6 ms | -0.56% | 4 | -2.3 |
| `--max-num-seqs 64`, graph sizes to 512 | 16 | ~39.2 ms | -0.12% | 4 | -0.6 |
| | 32 | ~53.0 ms | +0.14% | 8 | +1.9 (n.s.) |
| | 64 | ~78.2 ms | 0.00% | 4 | 0.0 |

At concurrency 32 the first 4 pairs read +0.24% (t = 3.3); a rerun of 4 more pairs read +0.03% (t = 0.3), so the pooled 8 pairs are within noise. As expected, the ~20-100 µs saved per step is a shrinking share of the step at high concurrency. The concurrency 8-64 runs load weights with `SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=0` (same for both arms) so server restarts reuse the page cache.

An earlier revision (which additionally replaced the full `paged_kv_indices.fill_(-1)` with a tail reset) measured -0.46% at concurrency 1 over 6 pairs (t = -4.7). That part was dropped to keep this PR small: the remaining `fill_` costs 7.8 µs per build.

Kernel and host numbers come from torch profiler traces of the serving run (decode builds inside the graph-replay window), with host time measured around `_build_decode` before profiling starts.

## Details

- The fused path is gated on full CUDA graphs, `self.dcp_world_size == 1` and no DCP total lengths; everything else keeps the existing code. A batch larger than the graph buffers is rejected by an assert (the eager ops rejected it too).
- `num_reqs` is excluded from Triton specialization (`do_not_specialize`) so new batch sizes do not trigger a JIT compile while serving.
- The kernel runs as a single program sized `next_power_of_2(max_num_reqs + 1)`: it writes kernel KV lengths and their zero-prefixed cumsum, the query indptr (uniform when padded), the tails up to the buffer length, and for varlen the q/o row maps.
- In the varlen case the row maps are left-aligned, which is always the case without DCP after #62990.
- `_expand_page_indices_kernel` now reads `kv_indptr` from the persistent buffer, which holds the same values as the old temporary.
- Gains are per decode step, so they matter most at low concurrency and with adaptive verification. The remaining biggest cost per build is AITER's own `get_mla_metadata_v1` (~28 µs), which this PR does not touch.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation and to run the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Stream Kimi K3 tool-call arguments
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust Kimi K3 parser buffers each `call` block until its close marker and decodes it at once, so a long argument produces no deltas until the call ends. This PR streams K3 arguments as they are generated, using the writer and call state added in the PR below.

## Claims

- The call name goes out when the call opens. A call without a tool name is still parsed and dropped, as before and as in the Python parser.
- A `type="string"` value streams as escaped JSON string fragments.
- A value of any other type is JSON text, written once complete, the same rule as DSML `string="false"` in the PR below: as spelled when it is valid JSON, as the renderer writes it, and otherwise as a JSON string of the text, as before and as in the Python parser.
- A raw `json` block streams as the whole arguments object, unchanged, as before: it has no per-value fallback, like native-JSON formats.
- `argument` and `json` markers are matched by token identity, so an ordinary-token spelling of `<|close|>argument<|sep|>` inside a value stays part of the value. This lifts the known limitation in the module docs, which Python shares.
- Behavior changes beyond chunking: valid non-string values keep their spelling instead of being decoded and re-serialized (`1.50` stays `1.50`), and a repeated argument keeps its first value.

## Validation

- New behavioral tests fail on the base and pass here: `kimi_k3_tool_call_streams_before_close_marker` (per-chunk progress), `kimi_k3_typed_arguments_keep_json_spelling_or_fall_back_to_strings` (`1.50` kept; malformed and empty values become strings), and `kimi_k3_ordinary_argument_close_inside_string_value_stays_value`. They replace `kimi_k3_tool_call_waits_for_close_marker` and `kimi_k3_malformed_typed_argument_falls_back_to_raw_text`, whose fallback case the new typed-argument test covers; the test helper now merges deltas per tool index.
- The Kimi K3 roundtrip case passes unchanged: its renderer writes compact values, which pass through inside a compact object.
- `cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server`, clippy with `-D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass, apart from the `vllm-server` test noted in the base PR, which fails the same way on main.
- Not covered: a run against a real model or engine.

## Details

- K3 uses the shared `OpenToolCall` with `JsonStyle::Compact`. A typed value is buffered to its close marker and written with `ArgumentsWriter::write_json`. The raw `json` block is appended with `ArgumentsWriter::push_raw_arguments`, and the object end is not written after one.
- The parser keeps a single `KimiK3Mode::Call` variant with a `CallBody` position (`Start`, `Arguments`, `Argument`, `TypedArgument`, `Json`, `AfterJson`), so the grammar's exhaustive mode match is unchanged. The XTML `index` attribute, which nothing used, is no longer read or stored.
- Complexity: about 247 non-test lines added and 123 removed; the whole-body decoding (`parse_call_arguments`, `typed_arguments`, `decode_argument_value`) is gone.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Match response_template regexes with PCRE2 in the hf parser
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The `hf` parser rejects `response_template`s whose boundaries use look-around, which includes the templates recently added to Qwen3.5+, Nemotron, Mistral, and GLM-5 checkpoints. This PR matches template regexes with PCRE2 and ports Transformers' `ResponseParser` scan onto it, instead of extending the `regex-automata` port. Related: vllm-project/vllm#65959 (RFC for a look-around-capable engine).

## Claims

- Every surveyed real template loads and parses like Transformers: 16 distinct templates from 134 Hub revisions with a `response_template`; 4 of them (91 revisions) fail to load on main, all on look-around.
- Template regexes now support whatever Python's `regex` accepts except unbounded lookbehind (`(?<=a+)`, a PCRE2 limit), including patterns without a literal prefix (`(?:^|<think>\s*)`) and `\Z`.
- Boundary decisions follow Transformers exactly (`_scan` / `_process` / `_can_grow`), including when a boundary commits, and `^` matches only at the start of the response; on main it matched at every candidate position.
- No `unsafe` and no new C dependency in vLLM: PCRE2 is already linked through `fastokens`.

## Validation

- Differential fixtures regenerated from Transformers `parse_response` at `c6329dd080`, adding the Qwen3.5, Mistral, GLM-5, Ernie, and Inkling templates and a zero-width chain (19 cases; the 21 existing expectations are unchanged). All pass whole and per character. On main the test fails at load: `regex "</think>|(?=<tool_call>)" is not supported by the Rust regex engine: ... look-around ... is not supported`.
- Single-boundary decisions in `template.rs` tests are checked against Python (`regex.search(..., partial=True)` plus `_can_grow`).
- Out of tree:
  - 8400 randomized outputs over 50 templates (Hub checkpoints, Transformers tests, local checkpoints), sampled from each template's own patterns, against Transformers, whole, per character, and in 5 random chunkings: no chunking-dependent result; every difference from Transformers is one of the parser's existing deliberate divergences (text fields without `repeats` concatenate their occurrences; prompt text produces no output).
  - 28,200 searches over the 47 surveyed template regexes (partial and complete, random start offsets) agree with Python `regex`, except 6 where `regex` misses a partial match (`[^>]*?` with `\b`).
- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-tokenizer`: 1248 passed; clippy clean.
- Streaming cost (release, 4-character chunks): 425–523 ns per chunk across Qwen3.5, GLM, Gemma 4, and Mistral outputs.

## Details

- **Why PCRE2:** Transformers decides streaming boundaries with Python `regex`'s `partial=True`, which reports a complete match anywhere before an earlier partial one (`abc|b` on `ab` finds `b`). That is PCRE2's `PCRE2_PARTIAL_SOFT`, and PCRE2 is a backtracking engine with the same look-around semantics. `regex-automata` has no look-around; `fancy-regex` has no partial matching or steppable automaton.
- **Executor:** `next_event` is `_scan` + `_process`: each watched boundary is searched from the current position with partial matching, a partial match or a complete one that may still grow holds the text from its start, and the preferred committable match is the earliest, then longest, opens before closes. Boundaries compile like `_compile_anchor` (escaped literal alternation with `can_extend`). `pattern.rs` (literal-prefix extraction, DFAs, assertion relaxing) is removed, and `hf` no longer scans for literal markers.
- **Context:** Transformers searches its never-trimmed buffer. The parser keeps the end of the consumed text, as many characters as the template's patterns look behind (`PCRE2_INFO_MAXLOOKBEHIND`, at least one), so lookbehinds and `\b` see consumed text and `^`/`\A` do not match mid-stream.
- **Zero-width boundaries** (`(?=<tool_call>)`) now fire; `parse_buffered_event` treated zero consumption as needing more input. When zero-width boundaries would repeat a scan at the same position (Transformers loops forever there), they are ignored until text is consumed.
- **Python dialect:** patterns compile with `UTF | UCP | DOTALL`; only `\Z` and `\uXXXX` / `\UXXXXXXXX` are translated. `xml-inline` tag patterns iterate with Python's (and Perl's) empty-match handling.
- **`pcre2` fork:** the `pcre2` crate does not expose partial matching (BurntSushi/rust-pcre2#12, open since 2020). This PR patches in [vllm-project/rust-pcre2](https://github.com/vllm-project/rust-pcre2/commits/master), a fork under the vLLM org that only adds API: match-time options (soft/hard partial with the partial match's position, `NOTEMPTY_ATSTART`), `max_lookbehind`, Perl-style iteration, match/depth/heap limits, partial JIT, and a CI job running the tests under AddressSanitizer with PCRE2 instrumented. `fastokens`' `pcre2 = "0.2"` resolves to the same fork, so the tree keeps one `pcre2` and one `pcre2-sys`; the `[patch]` goes once these land upstream.
- **Second commit:** the lax-JSON bare-key rewrite and the transform placeholder use `regex` instead of `regex-automata`, dropping that direct dependency of `vllm-parser`.
- **Limitations:** unbounded lookbehind, `\N{...}`, and `regex` V1 set operations are unsupported. No match limit is set beyond PCRE2's defaults.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Fail in-flight requests when an engine disconnects
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When an engine core dies without sending the `ENGINE_CORE_DEAD` sentinel (SIGKILL, the OOM killer, a segfault), the Rust frontend does not notice: in-flight requests hang and `/health` keeps reporting 200 until something outside the client tears the frontend down, and with engines on another node nothing ever does. This PR has the engine-core client detect the dead engine from the ZMQ transport itself.

## Claims

- In-flight requests fail with an error event within milliseconds of an engine process dying, instead of hanging until the frontend is killed or never ending.
- `/health` returns 503 right away, and later requests are rejected with the same error, exactly as after the sentinel.
- Detection is per transport connection, so it covers engines the frontend does not own (`--data-parallel-size-local 0`, engines on other nodes), not only a locally launched process.

## Validation

Unit test `engine_disconnect_fails_in_flight_requests_and_marks_client_unhealthy`: a mock engine receives a request, then drops its sockets without a sentinel; the in-flight stream must yield `EngineDisconnected` within 2s, the client must turn unhealthy, and a new request must be rejected. With the watch loop stubbed out, the test fails at the 2s timeout. `cargo nextest run` passes for the whole workspace.

End to end on one GB200, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `--shutdown-timeout 60`: start 4 streaming `/v1/completions` (`max_tokens=8000`, `ignore_eos`), wait until each has produced tokens, `SIGKILL` every `VLLM::EngineCore` process, then watch the streams, `/health`, and the frontend process for 90s. Times are seconds after the kill.

| Launch path | Build | 4 in-flight streams | `/health` | Frontend exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vllm-rs serve` | main | connection dropped at 61.8, no error | refused from 1.8 | 61.9 |
| | this PR | error event at 0.01 | 503 at 0.0 | 1.8 |
| `vllm serve` + `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` | main | connection dropped at 5.3, no error | refused from 0.3 | 6.5 |
| | this PR | error event at 0.01 | 503 at 0.0 | 1.5 |
| `vllm-rs serve --data-parallel-size-local 0` + `vllm serve --headless` | main | still open at 90 | 200 throughout | still running |
| | this PR | error event at 0.01 | 503 at 0.0 | still running (see Details) |

The error event is `{"message": "engine-core error: engine core EngineId(0000) disconnected", "type": "InternalServerError", "code": 500}`.

On main, `vllm-rs serve` notices the engine process exit right away, but the 4 requests stay registered against the dead engine (`Reqs Running: 4`), so graceful shutdown waits for the full 60s deadline before it drops them. Under `vllm serve`, the Python parent sees the engine exit and kills the frontend, which cuts the connections without an error.

## Details

Engines connect a DEALER to the client's shared input ROUTER under their engine index as identity and a PUSH to the output PULL. A connection closes when its process exits for any reason, but the output PULL socket neither reports closed connections nor knows which engine a connection belongs to; the input ROUTER does both. The client now subscribes to the input socket's monitor events and keeps polling its receive half (engines send nothing on it after registering, but zmq.rs only notices a closed connection while the socket is polled). The first `Disconnected` event for a registered engine is sent into the output channel as `Error::EngineDisconnected`, where the dispatcher handles it like the sentinel: it fails all registered requests and utility calls, records the health error, and publishes the client as unhealthy.

Losing any engine is fatal to the whole client, as the sentinel already is. The engine set is fixed after startup (elastic EP is not supported by the Rust frontend), and requests are not rerouted.

The Python client does not watch the transport. It relies on the sentinel, plus a process monitor when it launched the engines itself. A transient disconnect followed by libzmq's automatic reconnect under the same identity therefore goes unnoticed in Python, at the cost of silently dropping whatever was sent while the peer was gone. This PR has no reconnect grace window: after a reconnect, the client cannot tell whether requests or outputs were lost in between, so it fails instead of guessing.

Limitations:

- Only a closed connection is detected. A host crash, a network partition, or a hung engine leaves the TCP connection open and needs heartbeats or timeouts.
- An output already sent on the PULL socket can race with the disconnect event, the same race as between the sentinel and the last outputs.

Follow-up: with engines it does not own, the frontend keeps running and answers 503 after an engine dies. The Python API server exits in this case, through its watchdog `terminate_if_errored`, unless `VLLM_KEEP_ALIVE_ON_ENGINE_DEATH` is set. Matching that is a separate change.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][FLy][ROCm] Normalize the top-k entropy gate and allow a FLy cost overlay with synthetic acceptance
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

FLy's entropy gate now renormalizes the top-k target scores and divides by `log(k)`, so `fly_entropy_threshold` is a `[0, 1]` value with the same meaning for every `fly_entropy_top_k`. 

Setting `fly_window_size` with `rejection_sample_method="synthetic"` now runs FLy's entropy computation without deferring, so synthetic-acceptance benchmarks can pay FLy's verification cost at a pinned acceptance length. 

Follow-up to #53987.

## Claims

- **Normalized gate.** `compute_fly_entropy` returns the entropy of the renormalized top-k distribution divided by `log(k)`: 0 when the target is certain, 1 when the top-k candidates are equally likely. With the previous unnormalized gate, the ceiling grows with `k` (`log 3 = 1.10`, `log 40 = 3.69`) and depends on how much probability mass the top-k holds, so a threshold could not be compared across `fly_entropy_top_k`.
- **FLy cost overlay.** `synthetic` + `fly_window_size` keeps the synthetic acceptance decisions unchanged and adds only FLy's per-step entropy computation to verification.
- Standard, block, and synthetic-without-`fly_window_size` verification are unchanged.

## Validation

All runs: AMD MI355X ×8, TP=8, Kimi-K3 (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3@9f62e4e`) with `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark@48beb88`, `num_speculative_tokens=8`, greedy draft sampling, ModelRunner V2, `fly_window_size=2`, `fly_entropy_top_k=3`. "main + this PR" is the official ROCm nightly for `083fbac` with every `vllm/**/*.py` file replaced by this branch's (`main@8db73f2` + this PR; no `csrc/` change in between).

**Golden acceptance length** — SPEED-Bench `coding` (80 prompts), temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 4096 output tokens, concurrency 64; AL = 1 + Δaccepted / Δdrafts from `/metrics`; FLy with `fly_entropy_threshold=0.3`.

| vLLM | Standard AL | FLy AL | FLy gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | 4.093 (n=2) | 4.802 (n=2) | +17.3% |
| main + this PR | 4.101 ± 0.034 (n=3) | 4.878 ± 0.092 (n=3) | +18.9% |

**FLy cost overlay, after the change** — AgentX (`agentx-harness==1.0.13`, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`, 900 s, seed 42) on main + this PR, `synthetic_acceptance_length=4.802` (the FLy AL above). "alonly" is plain `synthetic`; "overlay" adds `fly_window_size=2, fly_entropy_threshold=0.3, fly_entropy_top_k=3`. Ratio = total time of the same completed requests, alonly / overlay (< 1 means the overlay is slower).

| Concurrency | Common requests | Overlay / alonly e2e | decode | Measured AL (alonly / overlay) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 53 | 0.9994 ± 0.0016 (2 nodes) | 0.9999 | 4.793 / 4.794 |
| 2 | 67 | 0.9969 | 0.9957 | 4.805 / 4.805 |
| 4 | 127 | 0.9945 (arms on different nodes) | 0.9924 | 4.805 / 4.803 |

The measured AL matches the pinned value in both arms, so the overlay never defers. At concurrency 4 the two arms ran on different nodes, so that ratio includes node-to-node variance (two other nodes differed by ≤ 0.2% at concurrency 1).

<details>
<summary>Evidence that the overlay runs (torch profiler, microbenchmark)</summary>

Live servers with the same config, 50 profiled decode steps each (`--profiler-config`, rank 0):

| op / kernel | synthetic | synthetic + `fly_window_size=2` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `_rejection_kernel` | 50 | 50 |
| `aten::topk` | 0 | 50 |
| `mbtopk::computeBlockDigitCounts` / `computeBlockwiseWithinKCounts` / `gatherTopK` | 0 / 0 / 0 | 200 / 200 / 50 |
| `aten::div` | 0 | 50 |

Direct `rejection_sample` calls (K=8, vocab 163840, fp32 logits): 200 seeded cases (temperature 0 and 1, 1–16 requests) are token-identical with and without the overlay; per-verify time goes from 0.108 to 0.217 ms for 1–8 requests. The compiled `_rejection_kernel` has the same 13 loads with and without the overlay (real FLy has 14, the extra one being the entropy load).

</details>

## Details

- **Overlay design.** It reuses the FLy path: `RejectionSampler` passes `fly_window_size` for `synthetic`, `rejection_sample` computes the entropy, and the kernel never starts a pending window when `SYNTHETIC_MODE` is set. Because `SYNTHETIC_MODE` is a constexpr, the deferral branch is compiled out in this mode, so the overlay pays the per-step entropy computation but not FLy's per-rejection window logic. `synthetic` with `fly_window_size` was previously accepted and silently ignored; it now enables the overlay. ModelRunner V2 only.
- **Tests.** No new tests are added. The existing FLy tests pass under both gate definitions.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open PR or issue changes FLy's entropy gate or combines FLy with synthetic acceptance (searched `FLy`, `fly_entropy`, `synthetic fly`). Open PRs touching `rejection_sampler_utils.py` (#65489, #65007, #65909) change unrelated paths.
- AI assistance was used to port the change and write the docs; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Resolve auxiliary frames of add requests in the mock engine
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm-mock-engine` never answers a request whose prompt has 64 tokens or more: since vllm-project/vllm#62702 the frontend sends such prompt token ids in an auxiliary ZMQ frame, and the mock engine drops every add request that is not exactly two frames. This decodes add requests with a new `EngineCoreRequest::from_frames`, which resolves every array sent in an auxiliary frame.

Replaces vllm-project/vllm#66353, which accepts the auxiliary frames without resolving them; its author is credited as co-author.

## Claims

- The mock engine serves long prompts again at the default `VLLM_MSGPACK_ZERO_COPY_THRESHOLD`.
- `EngineCoreRequest::from_frames` is the inverse of `EngineCoreRequest::extract_aux_frames`: prompt token ids, multimodal tensors, and `prompt_logprob_token_ids` come back resolved. The tests' scripted engines (`test_utils::decode_add_request`, which resolved only the prompt token ids) use it too.

## Validation

- New test `long_prompt_sent_in_aux_frame_is_served` (1024-token prompt): times out after 5 s on main, passes with this change. On main, a 63-token prompt is served and a 64-token one hangs.
- The two existing `extract_aux_frames` tests now also round-trip through `from_frames`.
- End to end with the Python frontend (`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size-local 0` plus the mock engine): a 1024-token completion request returns `finish_reason: length`, and short, streaming, and non-streaming requests behave as before.
- `cargo nextest run` for the engine-core client, mock engine, server, llm, and chat crates; clippy and fmt are clean.

## Details

Root cause: `EngineCoreRequest::extract_aux_frames` moves each array of at least `VLLM_MSGPACK_ZERO_COPY_THRESHOLD` bytes (256 by default, so a `uint32` prompt of 64 tokens) into a trailing frame, so an add request becomes `[type, payload, aux...]`. `decode_request` in `mock-engine/src/io.rs` rejected anything but two frames, logged a warning, and never replied.

Resolving the frames instead of only accepting them keeps the decoded request whole: an unresolved request still carries aux-frame indices in place of its arrays, which breaks anything that reads the values. The mock engine only reads the prompt length today; the follow-up that returns prompt logprobs needs the actual prompt token ids.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Shut down the executor when EngineCore fails to start
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When an in-process engine fails to start (e.g. "No available memory for the cache blocks"), its model stayed in device memory for the rest of the process. This PR shuts the executor down when `EngineCore`'s worker-side startup fails. This is what cascaded one failing test into three more in the Intel "Sleep Mode" job (intel-ci builds 17681 on #65708 and 17699 on main).

## Claims

- An in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) whose startup fails now releases its model before the error propagates.
- Engines in their own process behave as before. Shutting the executor down only runs earlier.

## Validation

New test `test_failed_inprocess_startup_releases_model`. An in-process `LLM` with about 1.6 GiB of dummy weights and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.001` fails startup, and the test then checks the process's allocated device memory. GB200:

```
# main
FAILED v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_failed_inprocess_startup_releases_model
E   AssertionError: assert 1988964352 < (256 * (1024 ** 2))
# this PR
PASSED v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_failed_inprocess_startup_releases_model
PASSED v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core
```

Finding the holder (GB200, main): after the failed startup, the next test in the process found 1.70 GiB still allocated after `gc.collect()` and `empty_cache()`. Every large tensor was reachable as below. With this PR the allocation drops to 0.03 GiB, with no large tensors left.

```
lm_head.weight <- ParallelLMHead <- TransformersMoEForCausalLM <- GPUModelRunner.model
  <- Worker.model_runner <- Worker._init_workspace_and_model_runner.<locals>.<lambda>
  <- WorkspaceManager <- vllm.v1.worker.workspace._manager
```

## Details

**Root cause.** `Worker` passes the workspace manager an `alloc_context` lambda that closes over the worker, and the manager is module-level state. Normally `free_before_shutdown` resets it, along with `static_forward_context`, `_ROPE_DICT` and the global graph pool. But that only runs from the model runner's `shutdown()`, and nothing called it when `EngineCore.__init__` raised after creating its executor. In a separate engine process the process exits, so it didn't matter. In-process, the worker, model runner and model stayed referenced until the process ended.

In the Intel job, `test_transformers_backend_weight_offloading[TitanML/tiny-mixtral]` failed startup in-process (see #67332). It left about 2 GiB allocated, and the three `test_transformers_backend_cpu_offload_outputs` tests that followed failed their startup memory check (12.46 GiB free, 13.92 GiB needed).

**Fix.** Wrap the worker-side startup steps after the executor is created (EEP scale-up, encoder output width measurement, KV cache initialization) and call `model_executor.shutdown()` before re-raising. A failure in that shutdown is logged so it doesn't replace the original error.

- **Why `BaseException`:** it also covers Ctrl-C during an in-process startup (e.g. in a notebook), where the process keeps running.
- **Engine processes:** `run_engine_core`'s signal handlers only record signals during construction, so this doesn't change how they handle SIGTERM/SIGINT.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Stop forwarding shutdown() to LMCache until it no longer aborts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stops `LMCacheConnectorV1.shutdown()` forwarding to the LMCache engine's `shutdown()`, and skips the test added with it. That forwarding (#64324) aborts the whole process in libzmq, which fails the "V1 KV Connectors" shards on main. Fixes #67121.

## Claims

- Engine shutdown with the LMCache connector no longer runs LMCache's `stop_services()`, so it can't abort the process in libzmq.
- `test_engine_shutdown_stops_lmcache_threads` is skipped until a fixed LMCache release can be required.

## Validation

Not run with LMCache; it's a revert of the forwarding in #64324. Pre-commit passes.

Failing CI before this change: the abort happens on main in builds 102164 and 102182, on MI355 (LMCache 0.5.3) and H200 MIG 35GB (LMCache 0.5.6).
```
LMCache INFO: Closing ZMQOffloadServer... (zmq_server.py:98)
LMCache INFO: ZMQ socket closed (zmq_server.py:104)
LMCache INFO: Waiting for offload server thread to finish... (zmq_server.py:110)
Assertion failed: pfd.revents & POLLIN (src/signaler.cpp:238)
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

## Details

**Root cause.** LMCache's `ZMQOffloadServer` runs a thread that blocks in `socket.recv()` with no timeout. `close()` sets `running = False` and then closes that socket from another thread to interrupt the `recv()`. ZMQ sockets are not thread-safe, so libzmq fails an internal assertion and aborts. `LMCacheLookupServer.close()` closes its transport the same way; its 1 s receive timeout makes the window smaller but doesn't close it. The code is the same in LMCache 0.5.3, 0.5.6, and its new home `LMCache/LMCache_inprocess`.

This isn't limited to the test. Since #64324, any clean shutdown with the LMCache connector (e.g. SIGTERM to `vllm serve`) runs this path and can dump core.

**Why skip rather than xfail.** The test aborts the pytest process, which a strict xfail can't catch. With the forwarding removed it would fail anyway.

**Tradeoff.** Without the forwarding, LMCache's non-daemon threads can again delay EngineCore's exit until it's force-killed (#62808). That's less harmful than aborting.

**Alternative considered.** vLLM could wake the blocked threads itself before forwarding: set `running = False`, send a dummy frame to the offload server's endpoint, join the threads, then call `shutdown()`. That reaches into private LMCache attributes, which differ between the `lmcache.v1` and `lmcache.inprocess.v1` packages. The right fix is in LMCache: the server thread should poll with a timeout or a stop signal and close its own socket, and `close()` should only signal and join. Forward `shutdown()` again once a release with that fix can be required.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: merge K2(l) and K1(l + 1) into one launch at TP8
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

At TP8 on MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode (`--monokernel`) launches K2 of layer l and K1 of layer l + 1 as one persistent kernel. This covers 34 of the 39 target layer boundaries and both DSpark draft boundaries. Each merged boundary saves the launch gap and K1's start-up.

## Results

- **Bit-exact.** Merged and separate launches give identical outputs on every rank in FULL-graph replays. The CI test below passes on MI355X on this branch.
- **Accuracy unchanged** (table below).
- **Perf.** Conc 1, 1 × TP8, DSpark k = 6: −96.8 µs per step (−2.21%), 4 ABBA pairs, SE 4.3 µs. The layer bench gives −1.71 to −2.08 µs per merged layer boundary. These perf numbers were measured before #63893, #64152, #64883 and #64153 merged;
- **Scope.** TP8 only. TP2, TP4 and gfx942 builds, and the standalone K1, K2 and FFN builds, are byte-identical to main. There is no new env var.

**Accuracy, main vs this PR**
- Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1 × TP8, `--monokernel`, DSpark k = 6 with real (block) acceptance, greedy.
- Every request runs at concurrency 1, so every decode step merges: about 150k target steps per PR session.
- ABBA order, 4 server sessions. Each arm's number is its two runs pooled.
- Both arms run the same nightly image. Main uses main's versions of the 8 files this PR changes.

| Task | main | PR | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (1319, 8-shot) | 91.24 | 91.85 | 0.22 |
| MATH-500 (4-shot) | 84.20 | 82.70 | 0.20 |
| RULER niah_multikey_3 / variable tracking, 4k–512k | 100 / 100 | 100 / 100 | – |
| RULER niah_single_2 / niah_multivalue, 4k–128k | 100 / 99.97 | 100 / 99.97 | – |
| RULER common words, 4k–512k | 97.60 | 97.35 | 0.18 |
| LongBench-v2 ≤ 120k tokens (294), direct answer | 52.2 | 52.4 | 1.0 |
| LongBench-v2 ≤ 120k tokens (294), chain of thought | 58.5 | 59.5 | 0.52 |
| Acceptance length, short / long tasks | 4.07 / 3.72 | 4.09 / 3.71 | – |

p is the paired McNemar test over both main/PR pairs. Outputs are not run-to-run deterministic on either side. Across all task × length cells, main/PR disagreement stays within main/main and PR/PR disagreement, and no cell differs after a Holm correction.

## How it works

- **No cross-CTA hand-off at the seam.** K2's MoE reduce task j, its FFN-seam slice j and K1(l + 1)'s seam slice j all run on CTA j. So K1's slice takes the MoE all-reduce in place of K2's reduce stage. Only K2's FFN-gate mixes cross CTAs, as tagged pairs.
- **When a boundary merges.** A layer defers its K2 only when the next layer is a whole mono layer of the same runner, with no torch op in between. That rules out the Engram boundaries 0→1 and 13→14 and the aux-capture layers 36–39.
- **Same decision on every rank.** The step's metadata decides.
- **Flush before any reader.** Anything else that reads a layer's outputs flushes the deferred K2 first.

## Tests

- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]` now also runs the model with merging on and off in FULL graphs. It checks that outputs are bit-equal on every rank and that there are 34 target and 2 draft merged launches. That case already runs in the MI355 TP8 CI step, so no CI config changes. It passes on MI355X in 623 s.
- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` adds CPU tests of the defer decision and of every flush.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Zero bubble draft tokens handoff for structured outputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow up to #63219 (cc @michael-gpu, @ArcheyChen)

~~Stacked on top of #66081, a bugfix for structured outputs + spec decode + async scheduling.~~  #66081 merged

Optimizes structured outputs + spec decode + async scheduling by removing bubbles in the scheduling pipeline.

## Claims

+3% E2E throughput at concurrency 64 compared to main on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with `dspark` spec decode for requests with structured outputs under async scheduling, pipeline-parallel (PP) =2, tensor-parallel (TP)=1.

No significant change or regression under sync scheduling or for TP=2, PP=1.

## Validation

Ran on B200.

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/cf366a45a21de10bcf364050656621cc
`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with `dspark` 7 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- 1 vs 64: low vs high concurrency

Async, TP=1, PP=2
```
python run.py --num-repeats 10 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --output <...>
```

Workload | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | Target tok/s | Change
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
Broad | 1 | 727.60 ± 0.50 | 732.30 ± 3.31 | +0.65%
Broad | 64 | 10,991.95 ± 101.22 | 11,105.82 ± 121.56 | +1.04%
Tight | 1 | 728.02 ± 0.53 | 735.48 ± 3.68 | +1.02%
Tight | 64 | 10,964.57 ± 125.17 | 11,258.04 ± 177.77 | +2.68%

Stat-sig gains on C64 cases.

Async, TP=2, PP=1
```
python run.py --num-repeats 10 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --output <...>
```

Workload | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | Target tok/s | Change
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
Broad | 1 | 854.71 ± 0.54 | 860.24 ± 3.10 | +0.65%
Broad | 64 | 15,225.78 ± 98.54 | 15,145.77 ± 121.25 | −0.53%
Tight | 1 | 850.02 ± 28.35 | 863.86 ± 2.63 | +1.63%
Tight | 64 | 15,216.80 ± 32.17 | 15,088.88 ± 105.45 | −0.84%

No stat-sig change.

```
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_draft_tokens_handler.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py

9 passed, 12 warnings

VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/utils_/test_gpu_sync_debug.py

22 passed, 24 warnings

VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py

1 passed
```

## Details

For strucutured output requests, the scheduler-side needs to know about the draft tokens proposed by the workers to compute grammar bitmasks and advance structured outputs grammar.

This is done via the `DraftTokensHandler`, which asynchronously copies draft tokens from the worker-side to the scheduler-side.

When async scheduling is used, the scheduler-side runs ahead of the workers and maintains a batch queue of pending batches, where `batch_queue_size = PP + 1`.

However, on main, `DraftTokensHandler` does not maintain a similar queue of copy synchronization barriers (CUDA events). It uses on barrier only, so the following can occur:
```
Scheduler-side                          Worker-side
---------------------------------------------------
Schedule Batch A with request `p`
                                        Run Batch A
Schedule Batch B
                                        Propose Batch A drafts and `DraftTokenHandler.set_draft_tokens`
                                        Run Batch B
Schedule Batch C with request `p`
                                        Propose Batch B drafts and `DraftTokenHandler.set_draft_tokens`
`DraftTokenHandler.get_draft_tokens` to get draft tokens from Batch A to compute request `p`'s grammar bitmasks.
```

The `get_draft_tokens` call in to get Batch A's draft tokens for Batch C races against the `set_draft_tokens` call from Batch B. Batch C cannot progress until Batch B's copy is complete, despite only needing Batch A's draft tokens. This introduces a pipeline bubble.

Under PP=1, this can occur but is rare. A running request will usually keep being scheduled in consecutive batches. However, skips can occur (see #66081), leading to bubbles.

Under PP>1, skips are not only possible but common. A decode request scheduled in batch `N` cannot be scheduled again until batch `N + PP`. This is enforced by `Request.next_decode_eligible_step`.

This is why E2E perf gains are only significant on PP>1 deployments.

The solution is to maintain one synchronization barrier per batch.

## Overview Revert the workaround from #59420. It copied the last column of the `(B, next_n)` context-length table before calling AITER's paged MQA logits, because AITER could not read the table then. ROCm/aiter#6451 fixed that; it is in AITER v0.1.27 and later, and main pins v0.1.29 (#66596). So the copy goes and `context_lens` is passed as is. ## Claims - With native MTP (`next_n > 1`), one less copy kernel per indexer layer per decode step (ROCm DSA indexer, Gluon and stage-1 calls). For `[B]` and `(B, 1)` lengths the helper was already a no-op. - Same logits as before. - Removes the helper's unit test with it; AITER tests the table in its own op test (`op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_pa_mqa_logits_2d_context_lens.py`, from ROCm/aiter#6451). ## Validation The paged MQA logits run once with the `(B, next_n)` table and once with the per-sequence lengths (contexts 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700, `next_n = 3`) give the same logits (gfx950; snippet under Details): | vLLM image | AITER | Same logits | | --- | --- | --- | | nightly `f5d93296c` (MI355X) | v0.1.29 (current pin) | yes | | nightly `f5d93296c` (MI350P) | v0.1.29 (current pin) | yes | | nightly `083fbac0` + this PR (MI355X) | v0.1.28.post1 | yes | | nightly `a2bcb565` + this PR (MI355X) | v0.1.27 | yes | End to end, GLM-5.3 (`amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) TP4 on MI355X, nightly `083fbac0` vs the same nightly + this PR. ROCm's DSA indexer decodes natively only up to `next_n = 2`: with MTP k=1 AITER gets the `(B, 2)` table (log: `use_flattening=False ... (next_n=2)`); with k=3 decode is flattened to `(B, 1)`, so the removed helper was a no-op there. | MTP k | Lengths AITER gets | Image | GPQA-Diamond (198) | RULER `niah_single_2` 64k | MTP accepted length | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `(B, 2)` | nightly | 0.899 | 1.0 | 1.76 | | 1 | `(B, 2)` | this PR | 0.899 | 1.0 | 1.79 | | 3 | `(B, 1)` | nightly | 0.894 | 1.0 | 2.57 | | 3 | `(B, 1)` | this PR | 0.899 | 1.0 | 2.70 | Accepted length is the median over log intervals. ## Details - Needs AITER v0.1.27 or later. With older AITER, native MTP brings back the fault #59420 worked around. - #60042 (draft) edits the same call; whichever lands second rebases.
Direct-call logits check (python3 same_logits.py in a ROCm vLLM image) ```python # Same call and arguments as vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py. import torch from aiter import dtypes from aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_mqa_logits import deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits torch.manual_seed(0) dev = "cuda" B, next_n, H, D, block = 4, 3, 32, 128, 64 contexts = [8192, 1500, 3000, 700] max_model_len = 8192 + next_n blocks_per_seq = (max_model_len + block - 1) // block num_blocks = B * blocks_per_seq q = torch.randn(B, next_n, H, D, device=dev).to(dtypes.fp8) weights = torch.randn(B * next_n, H, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32) kv = torch.randn(num_blocks, block, 1, D, device=dev).to(dtypes.fp8).view(torch.uint8) scale = (torch.rand(num_blocks, block, 1, 1, device=dev) + 0.5).view(torch.uint8) kv_cache = torch.cat([kv, scale], dim=-1).contiguous() # [blocks, 64, 1, D + 4] uint8 block_tables = torch.randperm(num_blocks, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32).view(B, blocks_per_seq) # (B, next_n): row j of request b sees contexts[b] - (next_n - 1 - j) keys table = torch.tensor( [[c - (next_n - 1 - j) for j in range(next_n)] for c in contexts], device=dev, dtype=torch.int32, ) last_col = table[:, -1].contiguous() # what #59420's helper passed def run(context_lens): out = torch.full((B * next_n, max_model_len), float("-inf"), device=dev) deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits( q, kv_cache, weights, out, context_lens, block_tables, max_model_len, ChunkK=256, Preshuffle=True, KVBlockSize=block, WavePerEU=2, ) torch.cuda.synchronize() return out print("same logits:", torch.equal(run(table), run(last_col))) ```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Clear cuBLAS workspaces at in-process shutdown to free the graph pool
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Clear ATen's cached cuBLAS workspaces at in-process `GPUModelRunner` shutdown. A workspace created during CUDA graph capture is allocated from the global graph pool and otherwise keeps that pool alive after its graphs are freed, so the next in-process engine's capture fails with `use_count > 0 INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED`.

This fixes the failure of `test_drafter_capture_writes_kv_only_to_the_null_block` (added in #66523) in the `V1 Executor + Worker` CI step on main since #67081, e.g. [build 102032](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102032#01a1ce17-2fc2-4401-bd5e-e34dac12bc55). #67201 targets the same failure by resetting the global graph pool id at shutdown. That avoids the assert but leaves the workspace stranded in the old pool. The two changes are complementary.

## Claims

- Fixes the `use_count > 0` assert when a Qwen3.5 (GDN) engine is shut down in process and another engine then captures CUDA graphs.
- Frees the 32 MiB workspace that was otherwise left in the graph pool after each such engine shuts down.

## Validation

On GB200 (torch 2.14.0), running the in-process engine tests from `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py` in sequence:

| | `test_adaptive_verification_profiles_against_the_final_cache` then `test_drafter_capture_writes_kv_only_to_the_null_block` |
|---|---|
| main | 1 passed, 1 failed (also fails in CI on main) |
| this PR | passed (with `test_capture_gets_the_memory_warmup_committed` before them: 3 passed) |

Live blocks left in the global graph pool after shutting down an in-process `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` engine, from `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` with allocation stacks recorded:

| | MTP + adaptive verification | MTP |
|---|---|---|
| main | 1 (32 MiB, allocated by `cuda_unquantized_gemm` from the GDN `in_proj_ba` lambda during breakable graph capture; no Python tensor refers to it) | 1 (same block) |
| this PR | 0 | not rerun |

## Details

Root cause:
1. `GatedDeltaNet` runs its small `in_proj_ba` GEMM on the global `aux_stream()` only while a graph is being captured, so that stream's first cuBLAS call always happens during capture.
2. ATen creates the cuBLAS workspace for each (handle, stream) lazily (32 MiB on SM90+). Because capture is in progress, it is allocated from the global graph pool, and ATen keeps it until `_cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces()`.
3. Before #67081, the compiled model's bytecode hooks leaked the model and its graphs at in-process shutdown, so the pool was never released. Now the graphs are freed and the pool's use count drops to 0, but the cached workspace keeps a live block in it, so the allocator cannot remove the pool. The next engine gets the same cached pool id from `get_global_graph_pool()` and asserts on capture.

PyTorch's inductor cudagraph trees clear these workspaces around recording for the same reason (`clear_cublass_cache()` in `torch/_inductor/cudagraph_trees.py`).

Limitations: the clear also drops workspaces allocated outside the pool. That only matters if another in-process engine on the device is still live, a case that shutdown already does not support (it resets the process-wide workspace manager and empties the allocator cache). The clear is limited to CUDA. ROCm was not tested and is left unchanged.

---

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Add a store trigger and isolated store trigger handlers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Phase 1 of #61396. Design comments belong in the RFC.

This PR gives the offloading manager the cause of each store, and moves the connector's store code into one handler per trigger. It adds `ON_HANDOFF` for state blocks that the KV cache manager hands off. The next PR adds `ON_OVERWRITE`, lets the manager select its triggers, and adds the `lazy` store mode.

This PR replaces #61426.

## Claims

- New `StoreTrigger` enum with `ON_COMPUTE` (the chunks are complete) and `ON_HANDOFF` (a state block is about to be reused, so the store cannot be postponed).
- `prepare_store` and `complete_store` take a required keyword-only `trigger`. `complete_store` also takes `success` keyword-only. An out-of-tree manager must add both parameters.
- The connector makes store jobs through a `StoreTriggerHandler` per trigger, in `offloading/store_triggers/`. Handlers offer keys and jobs through `StoreJobSink`. The scheduler owns the job ID, status, trigger stamp, fences, flushes and completion.
- Handlers are isolated: no handler knows of another, and each keeps its own state. The scheduler keeps global state and gives every handler the same hooks (`on_load_scheduled`, `on_request_removed`, `on_request_restarted`, `reset`, `first_live_chunk_idx`, `build_store_jobs`).
- `first_live_chunk_idx` returns the first chunk of a group whose GPU block ids a handler may still read, or `None` when it reads none. The scheduler zeroes stale sliding-window block ids only from the lowest value on.
- The scheduler adds `OnHandoffStoreHandler` whenever the config has a copy-on-write source group (`MambaSpec` with `mamba_cache_mode="align"`), before the manager's triggers. The job-ID order does not change, and the manager can decline these stores in `prepare_store`.
- The tiering manager gives the trigger to its primary tier. A promotion is not a store, so `prepare_write` and `complete_write` are real methods.

## Validation

- Every commit carries a `Signed-off-by`. `pre-commit run` passes on the merge commit below, including ruff and mypy.
- Merged `main` `f0787a9ab8` on 2026-11-12. The merge absorbs the DCP partial-tail rules for hybrid models (#58619), the pending-state reset on a required group miss (#67152), the ARC running-request eviction order (#67098), and lookahead block hashes for the remaining KV connectors (#65448). The store side now lives in `OnHandoffStoreHandler`: it derives the checkpoint boundary with `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position` and addresses each group's own block size. `SchedulerOffloadConfig` gains `cache_hit_alignment_tokens` and `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block`, and its DCP-aware `supports_partial_tail` replaces the old uniformity and DCP-width checks.
- The `#65448` changes land in two places. `scheduler.py` keeps `self.num_hash_lookahead_tokens` and derives `use_lookahead_block_hashes` from it. The retention boundary `num_prompt_tokens - max(1, num_hash_lookahead_tokens)` lives in `store_triggers/candidates.py`, where `select_store_candidates` is the only store-path user, and only `OnComputeStoreHandler` calls it. `OnHandoffStoreHandler` is additive: it takes its boundaries from the scheduler's handoff entries, so it has no copy of that logic. `OffloadingConnector.supports_lookahead_block_hashes` is gone, because the base class default is now `True`.
- At the merged tip `c618ca51bf`:
    - `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`: 519 passed, 12 failed.
    - every other file in the same directory (`--ignore=test_scheduler.py`): 227 passed, 2 skipped.
    - `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py`: 86 passed.
- All 12 failures are host limits, and each fails the same way on unmodified `main`. 6 are `test_cache_reset*`, which need `/dev/shm`, and macOS does not have it. 6 are `test_lookahead_partial_*`, which need Triton for speculative decoding, and the standalone CPU model runner rejects them without it. The full-suite run at the earlier head `8e0158e016` reported 1614 passed, 13 skipped and 17 failed, all of the same two host limits. `test_shared_offload_region.py` and `test_gpu_worker.py` are deselected for the same reason.
- The 11 pre-merge commits each pass `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py`.
- An earlier rebase onto `main` `8551e3a13f` (2026-11-11) absorbed three upstream behaviors: lookahead block hashes suppress the EAGLE tail drop (`apply_eagle_drop`) and the EAGLE peek in the reachable store mask, and a store spec keeps null pages inside a chunk as placeholders. The reachable-mask guard was missed in an earlier rebase and is now covered by `test_reachable_store_mask_skips_eagle_peek_with_lookahead_hashes`.
- End-to-end sanity, one H100 per model, 0 server errors. Measured at head `8e0158e016`, which predates the `main` merge, so a re-run on the merged tip is still pending; Qwen base `8551e3a13f`; image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.34.0rc1.dev206`):

| model | workload | side | req/s | mean TTFT ms | TPOT ms | store GB | load GB | hits |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B | client.py 32x3188, 3 rounds | head | - | - | - | 29.82 | 0.009 | 0.03% (R3) |
| Qwen3-8B | client.py | base | - | - | - | 29.82 | 0.009 | 0.03% (R3) |
| Qwen3-8B | prefix_repetition 48x4096 | head | 48.97 | 162.8 | 17.95 | - | - | - |
| Qwen3-8B | prefix_repetition | base | 48.51 | 169.4 | 18.06 | - | - | - |
| Falcon-H1-0.5B (align) | client.py 32x3332, 3 rounds | head | - | - | - | 4.52 | 2.38 | 90.0% (R3) |
| Falcon-H1-0.5B (align) | prefix_repetition 32x4096 | head | 16.98 | 436.3 | 19.12 | - | - | - |

- The Qwen client counters are identical on both sides: 29.822 GB stored, 9.4 MB loaded, 64 external hits and 100800 GPU prefix hits on 205741 queries. This base and image keep the working set in the GPU prefix cache, so the CPU tier barely serves it; the comparison is still like for like.
- Falcon handlers are `['ON_HANDOFF', 'ON_COMPUTE']`, with CoW source group 1 (`MambaSpec`). A measurement-only wrapper counted 432 offers, 352 keys and 352 jobs under `ON_HANDOFF`; `ON_COMPUTE` took 370 offers, 618 keys and 337 jobs. `ON_COMPUTE` skips `requires_cow_source` groups, so the Mamba state can reach the CPU tier only through the handoff path.
- Caveat: greedy text is not bit-stable after a CPU restore. Falcon head matched 24 of 32 rounds, and a no-offload control matched 32 of 32 on the same prompts. Qwen matched 31 of 32 on both head and base, with the same prompt diverging. On the 2026-11-01 run, with byte-identical offload counters, Falcon matched 29 of 32 on head and 30 of 32 on base. The drift is in the Mamba-align CPU-restore path, predates this PR, and I have not root-caused it.

CI runs these tests in `v1/kv_offload` and `v1/kv_connector/unit`. The KV-Offload lm-eval jobs also trigger on these paths.

## Compatibility

`prepare_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger)` and `complete_store(keys, req_context, *, trigger, success)` break out-of-tree managers. That is the only break. There is no user-visible config change.

Eager behavior is unchanged. The aligned-boundary and partial-tail stores keep the same source, the same keys and the same job-ID order. They now live in `OnHandoffStoreHandler`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to write the code, the tests and this text. I reviewed each changed line and can explain each design choice.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][HiSparse] Batch the coordinator's per-page residency bookkeeping
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The HiSparse coordinator updated residency one page and one resident group at a time, with a block-pool call per block. When a request's whole context is GPU-resident (~1.3k pages × 20 groups), one `schedule()` spends tens of ms in Python and stalls every running request. #65888 promotes completed P/D imports into GPU-resident pages, which makes that the common case on decoders.

This PR batches each operation (adopt, unpin, writeback planning and completion, copy recording, free) into one pass per request and one block-pool call: for a fully resident request (~1.3k pages × 20 groups), each operation goes from ~26k single-block pool calls and residency lookups to one pool call and one lookup per group. `HiSparseResidentManager` gains `get_residency_pages`, `adopt_resident_pages` and `drop_resident_pages`, which touch only the requested pages, so per-step cost does not grow with context length. Behavior is unchanged, including the order blocks return to the free queue; two new tests pin that order.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these loops.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py`
- GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, concurrency 128) with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 2G` to force host offload.
- Non-P/D and P/D host landing: 8×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, multi-turn agentic dataset (80K-token first turn, 13 turns), C=8, N=16, 220 output tokens, fresh servers per point, two dataset offsets per arm. P/D: 1P + 1D, TP4 each, NIXL over RDMA.
- P/D with GPU promotion (#65888): GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 1P1D on 2×GB300 nodes (TP4 each), decoder on `MultiConnector[NixlConnector, HiSparseConnector]`, NIXL over RDMA; multi-turn 64K (8 conversations, C=8) and GSM8K 5-shot.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: no new failures; the failures here match `main` on the same host.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Elastic EP] Recreate stat loggers before starting new engines
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes a hang on elastic EP scale-up caused by #60001: the stat loggers are now recreated for the new engine count *before* the new engines start, not after.

Failing test: `distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling` ([amd-ci build 15809](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15809#01a1cb30-f116-4364-bdf7-fabe78caac18), the first build with #60001).

## Claims

- Scale-up no longer kills the output handler with `KeyError` in `PrometheusStatLogger.record`.
- New engines' startup scheduler gauges (the goal of #60001) are recorded, not dropped.

## Validation

MI300 (4x gfx942), in the failing build's CI image (`rocm/vllm-dev:build-01a1cae8-8cb5-4282-82c5-c6070c1f0ced`, vLLM 3c5cdcfee7):

```bash
cd /vllm-workspace/tests && pytest -v -s distributed/test_elastic_ep.py -k test_elastic_ep_scaling
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before (3c5cdcfee7) | 4 failed, 1 skipped: `KeyError` on every failure |
| After (3c5cdcfee7 + this PR's commit) | 4 passed, 1 skipped |

`cuda_graphs_heavy_nixl_ep` skips in both runs (NIXL EP not in the image, as in CI). Not run on NVIDIA; the change is platform-independent frontend code.

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

Before:
```
(APIServer pid=1575) WARNING 11-11 17:54:22 [loggers.py:461] Unexpected engine_idx: 2
(APIServer pid=1575) ERROR 11-11 17:54:22 [async_llm.py:952] KeyError: 2
(APIServer pid=20608) WARNING 11-11 17:59:26 [loggers.py:461] Unexpected engine_idx: 2
(APIServer pid=20608) ERROR 11-11 17:59:26 [async_llm.py:952] KeyError: 2
(APIServer pid=39170) WARNING 11-11 18:04:22 [loggers.py:461] Unexpected engine_idx: 3
(APIServer pid=39170) ERROR 11-11 18:04:22 [async_llm.py:952] KeyError: 3
(APIServer pid=57676) WARNING 11-11 18:11:25 [loggers.py:461] Unexpected engine_idx: 2
(APIServer pid=57676) ERROR 11-11 18:11:25 [async_llm.py:952] KeyError: 2
FAILED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[enforce_eager_none]
FAILED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[enforce_eager_light]
FAILED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[enforce_eager_heavy]
FAILED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[cuda_graphs_heavy]
distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[cuda_graphs_heavy_nixl_ep] SKIPPED
============ 4 failed, 1 skipped, 16 warnings in 1550.54s (0:25:50) ============
```

After:
```
============ 4 passed, 1 skipped, 16 warnings in 1370.56s (0:22:50) ============
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Since #60001, every engine core sends its scheduler stats at startup. `_scale_elastic_ep` started the new engines (`prepare_elastic_ep()`) and only then recreated the loggers, so:

1. `prepare_elastic_ep(4)` starts engines 2 and 3, which send their startup stats.
2. The output handler records them with the old logger manager, which covers engines 0 and 1.
3. `LoggingStatLogger` warns `Unexpected engine_idx`; `PrometheusStatLogger.record` raises `KeyError`, the output handler dies, and the test times out.

Before #60001, new engines did not report until they served requests, after the loggers were recreated.

**Fix.** Move `prepare_elastic_ep()` below the existing logger recreation; the recreation code is unchanged. Making `PrometheusStatLogger` skip unknown engines instead would hide the ordering bug and drop the new engines' startup gauges.

**Failed scale-up.** The loggers now already cover the new engine count if `prepare_elastic_ep()` fails. That is kept on purpose: engines started before the failure may still send stats, and loggers rolled back to the old count would raise the same `KeyError`.

**CI gap.** Neither step that runs `test_elastic_ep.py` (`(MI300) Elastic EP Scaling`, `(H100) [Nightly] Elastic EP Scaling`) lists `vllm/v1/engine/` in `source_file_dependencies`, so it ran neither for #60001 nor for this PR. Adding it would put a 4-GPU job on many PRs; leaving that to maintainers.

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review (it changes how seven jobs are scheduled).

Enroll seven jobs in automatic runtime sharding. Two of them are long enough that the planner splits them; the other five fit in one job today and shard without another PR when their tests grow.

## Claims

| Job | Command shape | Planned shards |

| `amd-kimi-k3-prefix-cache-4xb200` (AMD mirror; base already enrolled) | connector check, then one pytest file | 3 |
| `amd-moriio-write-dummy-e2e-mi355` (standalone AMD) | connector check, `export`, then one pytest file with `-k`; drops its fixed 6-way `--shard-id` split | 4 |

| `amd-mamba-ssm-kernels-mi355` (standalone AMD) | two pytest files | 1 |

## Validation

- The pipeline generator plans every job from main's timings; none is ignored. The planned sharding cost (setup repeated per extra shard) is within 4% of one job for the two split jobs.
- Every job passed all of its recent main and nightly runs.
- The local shard harness runs every test of the two split jobs exactly once, in PR and main (OTel) mode.
- `split_check.py`: no multi-job step runs its whole suite in every job.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run the NIXL PD tests as pytest and enroll every Disaggregated step
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review (it changes the commands of 12 NVIDIA steps, their AMD mirrors and 7 AMD steps in `test-amd.yaml`).

## Overview

Follow-up to #66196, which did the same for the per-PR core sweep. The Disaggregated steps run bash scripts, so CI's automatic sharding can't plan them. Four nightly 4-GPU sweeps take over 30 minutes as one job. This PR runs every Disaggregated step's script through pytest and enrolls all of them and their AMD mirrors:

- The two config sweeps become pytest files with one test per config, so the planner can spread the configs over jobs by measured time.
- Each step that runs one script once gets a one-test wrapper. It stays one job, but it is enrolled, and main records its timing.

## Claims

- Every caller runs the same scripts as before, with the same environment, flags and order.
- `config_sweep_accuracy_test.sh` (pull mode) becomes `test_accuracy_sweep.py`. The step's environment still picks the group (`DP_EP`, `HYBRID_SSM`, `SW_ATTN`, else the TP configs) and the serve flags (`ATTENTION_BACKEND` / `ROCM_ATTN` / `FLASHINFER` for `--attention-backend`, `CROSS_LAYERS_BLOCKS` for `--enable-cross-layers`). The Distributed step's separate sleep/wake line becomes one more test (`test_pd_accuracy[sleep-wake]`) in the plain TP sweep only.
- `nixl_push_integration/config_sweep_accuracy_test.sh` becomes `test_push_accuracy_sweep.py` in the same folder, with the same 2 configs and no flags.
- `test_pd_scripts.py` has one test per single-run script: `test_accuracy` (`run_accuracy_test.sh`, for DSv4-Flash and Kimi-Linear), `test_edge_cases`, `test_mamba_prefix_cache`, `test_multi_connector_accuracy` and `test_multi_connector_edge_cases`. Each step runs its test by node ID, and the step's environment reaches the script unchanged.
- The NIXL import canary moves from inside the sweep scripts to a setup line (`python3 -m pytest`), so it still runs first in every job.
- Enrolled (`automatic_shard: true`): every Disaggregated step except the NIXL core sweep (#66196), and every AMD mirror. Timeouts are unchanged.
- In `test-amd.yaml`, the 6 pull-sweep lines and the push-sweep line make the same swap; its single-run script lines stay on bash, since those jobs can't take automatic sharding.

## Validation

- Differential checks against stub scripts that record which script ran, its environment and arguments. The old callers and the new tests make the same calls in the same order for:
  - every pull-sweep caller environment in the YAML (5 NVIDIA, 4 AMD), plus `SW_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN`;
  - both push callers, with a config value winning over the same variable in the step's environment, as before;
  - each single-run script with an empty environment, with the AMD prefixes, and with the DSv4-Flash mirror's prefixes, empty `*_KV_LAYOUT=` values included.

  A failing config or script fails its own test. Node IDs are pinned.
- Mutation testing of the three new files against those checks: all mutants killed.
- pre-commit passes on the changed files.
- Planner: every enrolled step and mirror passes its command check. The four long sweeps plan Distributed 3 jobs, FlashInfer 2, CrossLayer 2, Hybrid SSM 3 from treatment build 101613's timings. The MI355 AITER mirror already ran pytest on main and its timings plan one job. Every other step and mirror has no main timings yet, so it runs as one job, as today, until a main run times it.
- `/ci run` build 101618 (previous head, sharded sweeps): Distributed 3 jobs (slowest 15.8 min), FlashInfer 2 (17.4), CrossLayer 2 (17.3), Hybrid SSM 3 (17.0). Against 101613, every step ran the same node IDs, all passed, with 0 missing, added, changed or duplicated. Machine time +4% to +7%, and +12% for Hybrid SSM (two extra setups, plus the first config in each job starting cold).
- `/ci run` build 102157 and scoped build 102170 (the two optional MI355 mirrors), head 9b3e8ffb47 rebased on main f0787a9ab8: all 24 enrolled jobs passed, with no retries. Against main's latest nightly (102057), every job ran the same inner pytest runs with the same results (matched by pytest summary lines, since the old jobs ran their inner pytest without `-v`). Machine time is within ±10% for every job. The four long sweeps sharded 3/2/2/3 within the 20-minute target. Every other job ran as one job, as on main, until main times it. The previous head's builds (101826, 101827, against nightly 101548) gave the same results line for line.
- Not run: the `test-amd.yaml` lines run in the AMD pipeline, not in these builds. Each is the same swap as its mirror's line.

## Details

- **Mode from the environment, not `-k`.** Keeps every YAML change to one swapped line and the AMD callers identical in shape; the env names are the scripts'.
- **One-test wrappers for single-run scripts.** Rewriting their server start-up as pytest fixtures would be a much bigger change. Running the script keeps behaviour identical, and a later rewrite can split them.
- **Push stays in its own folder,** so push coverage can still grow on its own. `run_accuracy_test.sh` resets `ATTENTION_BACKEND` and only reads the `--attention-backend` flag, so the MI300 push mirror's `ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN` has no effect, before and after; this PR doesn't change that.
- **No `-x`.** The bash loops stopped at the first failing config; pytest runs the rest, so one nightly reports every broken config.
- **Hybrid SSM stays enrolled at +12% machine time** (+9% against the latest nightly): about 4.6 extra minutes per night for a step that finishes about 21 minutes sooner.
